item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Yankees prospect Dax Kilby's swing change fuels remarkable Arizona Fall League rise
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: New York Yankees top 2025 draft pick Dax Kilby entered the 2026 season with all the helium in the world coming off a pro debut that featured top-tier exit velocities and remarkable maturity. item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees top 2025 draft pick Dax Kilby entered the 2026 season with all the helium in the world coming off a pro debut that featured top-tier exit velocities and remarkable maturity. Somehow, he almost lost the entire campaign as a potential canvas for his artistry, felled multiple times by hamstring issues and hidden in the shadows.
Thankfully, he returned towards the end of the year, though he only appeared in 32 games in total (at the same level in Tampa), posting an impressive .883 OPS (.261 average, remarkable .448 OBP). No, he didn't get to strut his stuff in front of a higher level of competition at High-A Hudson Valley like we'd hoped, but that's what the Arizona Fall League is for - and Kilby's remained healthy and in the spotlight this October.
Thus far, Kilby has posted a .290 AVG, .613 SLG%, and .964 OPS in what's essentially a league of All-Stars and standouts who need additional reps entering pivotal offseasons. He's tallied seven extra-base hits and only struck out four times (music to some fans' ears).
Kilby's new swing has been on display, and is meant to ease his adjustment to pro ball and reduce his ground ball rate. He's starting both narrower and more open than he did in 2025, aimed at helping him with pitch recognition and getting the bat path where it needs to be quicker. Though you can't really be disappointed with the productivity of any Kilby swing, old or new, it's safe to say the new approach has cracked through the ceiling somewhat - and he's only 19.
Dax Kilby's Yankees future could involve a fast rise (and solve a major roster problem) if he stays healthy
The Yankees lack a long-term second baseman and George Lombard Jr. double play partner, as much as we hope Anthony Volpe continues to take steps forward in 2027 and beyond (while also hoping that Lombard Jr. firmly locks down the job instead of merely raising our eyebrows). Kilby could continue advancing into that role - and if he does arrive, he'll bring a keen eye and level of on-base skills that the Yankees have sorely lacked in recent years.
Back when getting on base was a Moneyball innovation, the Yankees took firm advantage of it, patiently taking their walks and turning solo shots into three-run homers. Somehow, while fans clamor for contact hitting and old-school prowess, the Yankees got away from what really made them great: reaching base. New York ranked 24th in OBP this season, and while Aaron Judge's absence affected things ... let's put it bluntly: that can never happen again. Kilby's been an on-base machine so far in his young career, and while the metrics and power will make more noise, that talent is something the Yankees desperately need, and that he might be able to provide in two years or less. This stint in the AFL has certainly proven that he's not to be trifled with as a future cog.

item.content:encoded:
It was clear even after the New York Mets signed Jorge Polanco that first base remained a sore spot on the roster. It's nearly impossible to replace Pete Alonso, of course, but the front office hardly put their best foot forward in trying to do so in 2026.
As a team, the Mets accrued the worst fWAR (-1.4) from first basemen in the league this season. The struggles of Polanco and Mark Vientos played a big part in that, but it's also worth noting that Jared Young did his best to stabilize the position when he was called upon. A .266/.330/.429 (111 wRC+) slash line isn't going to make anyone forget about Alonso, but it does give David Stearns and company something to build around at the cold corner.
Of course, anyone who watched the Mets over the course of the year was privy to a clear problem: Young is made for a platoon. As great as he was against right-handed pitching (.793 OPS, 120 wRC+), he was completely untrustworthy against southpaws (.606 OPS, 72 wRC+). Naturally, that has fans itching for the team to sign a lefty-masher to join Young at first base in 2027.
Does that mean the organization could make a play for someone like Ty France in free agency?
Mets have the money, but not the role, to lure Ty France away from Padres
The appeal of France is obvious; he's a Gold Glove winner at first base who just experienced his best offensive season ever in a breakout role for the San Diego Padres. He hit 21 homers and posted a 141 wRC+ in 500 plate appearances, hammering both righties (.869 OPS) and lefties (.853 OPS). SNY identified him as a perfect "under the radar" free agency fit for the Mets this offseason.
The problem isn't so much the player himself, but rather what the Mets can offer him. Money shouldn't be an issue -- the Padres, even with new ownership in tow, are dealing with serious financial constraints -- but playing time would be. France established himself as a fan-favorite star in 2026 on a playoff-caliber team. To leave that comfort in favor of a platoon role on a retooling squad in New York likely won't have much appeal.
Again, money could be the great equalizer here. But France, who was openly mulling retirement last year, is going to want the security that comes with a starting job. He has no need for a change of scenery, regardless of the amount of dollars that are offered to him by interested clubs.
Besides, there are other players who fit the platoon description the Mets are looking for better. For instance, Paul Goldschmidt has been excellent in that role in recent years, and he'd fill David Stearns' annual quota of poaching Yankees players.

item.title: [si.com] Aaron Boone Must Change the Yankees’ Culture to Take the Next Step
item.dc:creator: Karl Rasmussen
item.description: “Run it back” is a phrase Yankees fans have heard far too many times over the last few years. Reports emerged Monday evening indicating that manager Aaron Boone would be back in his role next season, marking his 10th season at the helm in the Bronx. item.content:encoded:
“Run it back” is a phrase Yankees fans have heard far too many times over the last few years. And it’s one they’ll be hearing again as it relates to the manager position heading into the 2027 season.
Reports emerged Monday evening indicating that manager Aaron Boone would be back in his role next season, marking his 10th season at the helm in the Bronx. Despite a tremendously disappointing no-show by the Yankees in the ALDS against the rival Rays, Boone’s return to the organization always felt like the most likely outcome.
Boone has been the Yankees’ manager since 2018. He owns a 790–565 record in the regular season and has led the team to the postseason in eight of his nine years as the skipper. In the playoffs, however, he has a 27–30 record and has reached the World Series just once despite making four trips to the ALCS. It’s now been 17 years since New York has claimed a World Series title, which is the longest drought in franchise history.
Frustration among the fan base has never been higher, and there’s no shortage of impatience with Boone’s inability to produce a championship throughout his tenure. Still, owner Hal Steinbrenner continues to express belief that Boone is the right man for the job, despite the fan base longing for a change in leadership and making that abundantly clear with the “Fire Boone” chants that rang out across Yankee Stadium during Game 3, shortly before the Rays celebrated their series win on the Yankees’ field.
Fans aren’t the only ones that have been critical of Boone’s Yankees. In the aftermath of their humiliating defensive performance in the ALDS against the Rays, franchise legends such as Derek Jeter and Alex Rodriguez have been vocal about the team’s appalling fundamentals and the need for an improved clubhouse culture.
“We’ve been watching the same movie for over a decade, and nothing changes,” Rodriguez said on Fox’s postgame show after the Yankees were swept by the Rays.
It’s been the same recipe for the Yankees throughout Boone’s tenure. The team prioritizes power at the plate, frequently ranking among the top teams in home runs and slugging. This year, with Aaron Judge on the shelf for more than half of the regular season, they leaned more on their elite pitching to navigate the regular season. But their deficiencies remain true; the team continues to struggle with fundamentals, particularly on defense, the lineup is strikeout prone and overly reliant on home runs, and despite assembling a roster worth north of $300 million, there are still some glaring holes at the bottom of the lineup. Just about every year, the Yankees start strong, slump over the summer, reach the postseason and are outmatched by a more complete team in October. This year, that team happened to be the Rays, who, along with the Brewers, showcased why thorough roster construction is far more important than throwing money at big names in free agency.
The team’s inability to win in different ways has been a thorn in their side under Boone, too. And it’s a big part of the reason he is the only Yankees manager in history to be in his role for more than five years and still not win a single World Series. Boone has enabled the Yankees to coast by off of their power at the plate, but they often struggle to convert with runners in scoring position, which makes it difficult for the team to rally back in games in which the home run ball hasn’t been a factor. The team ranked 22nd in RBIs with runners in scoring position and 18th with a .246 batting average in such situations. The little things, both offensively and defensively, haven’t been hammered home enough during Boone’s tutelage, and that presents itself in October on a semi-regular basis.
“We were teams that focused on all the little things. We would beat you with a home run, but we’d also beat you 2–1,” Jeter said of Yankees teams during his tenure throughout the late 1990s and 2000s. “There’s different ways of winning games when you’re not swinging the bats well. But we didn’t beat ourselves, and I think in this particular series, there are a lot of games where the Yankees beat themselves.”
Boone is entering the final year of his contract, so there’s a real chance that the two sides will part ways at the conclusion of the 2027 season, barring a new deal being reached. Considering there’s a possible lockout looming, one that could extend well into the regular season, it’s not a huge surprise that Boone wasn’t let go. Navigating a managerial change while the league is locked out is an extremely difficult task because all club business must be halted. That would limit the amount of time Boone’s replacement had to get familiarized with the clubhouse and implement the changes necessary to turn things around for the team.
The potential for a lockout likely worked in Boone’s favor as it pertains to his job, but unless he shows some dramatic signs of improvement, the ‘27 season may well be his last. Bringing Boone back without a new deal in place will also create a new sense of urgency. He’s a lame duck heading into next year, which will put some pressure on him to get the most out of this team and finally get over the hump and back to the World Series.
Boone needs to make some changes his to approach as manager. The team is “stuck in a rut,” as put by former pitcher C.C. Sabathia, and it’s long past time Boone made an active effort to alter the clubhouse culture by holding players accountable for their shortcomings and honing in on the fundamentals to bring this team back to its glory days.
This is a Yankees team that is consistently very good, having earned eight playoff berths in nine years, but they haven’t taken the steps necessary to be great, reaching the World Series just once in that span before getting outclassed by the Dodgers in 2024. Boone’s seat is hot, yet he’s secured himself one more season to try to get New York back in the Fall Classic. Failure to do so should mark the end of his time in the Bronx.
Karl Rasmussen is a staff writer for Sports Illustrated. A University of Oregon alum who joined SI in February 2023, his work has appeared on 12up and ClutchPoints. Rasmussen is a loyal Tottenham, Jets, Yankees and Ducks fan.
Follow Karlras920

item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Los Yankees toman una decisión final sobre Aaron Boone tras el colapso en los playoffs
- MLB. Dos jugadores de los Rays celebran con un saludo por todo lo alto tras ganar en la ALCS
Otro año sin título de Serie Mundial significa otro fracaso para los New York Yankees. El equipo dirigido por Aaron Boone volvió a quedarse corto en su objetivo después de ser barrido por los Tampa Bay Rays en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana (ALDS) a principios de este mes.
La eliminación llegó con una derrota por 4-3 en el Juego 4 disputado en el Yankee Stadium, un golpe que terminó con las altas expectativas que rodeaban a la franquicia antes de la postemporada.
Alex Rodríguez se equivocó con su pronóstico sobre los Yankees
Uno de los que más confianza tenía en los Yankees era la leyenda de la organización, Alex Rodríguez.
Antes del inicio de los playoffs, el exjugador pronosticó que Nueva York llegaría a la Serie Mundial de 2026 e incluso levantaría el trofeo.
“Voy con los Yankees venciendo a los Dodgers en una revancha de hace un par de años. Son los dos mejores cuerpos de pitcheo del juego. Me quedo con ellos. Pitcheo y defensa”, dijo Alex Rodríguez.
Sin embargo, la predicción de Rodríguez quedó muy lejos de cumplirse. Los Yankees no pudieron superar la ALDS y ahora deberán esperar al menos una temporada más para intentar terminar con una sequía de Serie Mundial que sigue creciendo.
Una temporada sólida que terminó en decepción
Aunque el cierre fue amargo, Nueva York tuvo una buena temporada regular al finalizar con récord de 93-68 en 161 partidos, resultado que le permitió terminar en el segundo lugar del Este de la Liga Americana.
Además, los Yankees barrieron a los Boston Red Sox en la Serie de Comodines, aumentando la ilusión de regresar al Clásico de Otoño por primera vez en varios años.
Pero los Rays terminaron con esas aspiraciones y dejaron nuevamente a una de las franquicias más exitosas en la historia del béisbol sin el campeonato que sigue buscando.
A pesar del decepcionante cierre de la temporada 2026, todo apunta a que Aaron Boone regresará como manager para un año más. Cabe recordar que los Bombarderos del Bronx no ganan una Serie Mundial desde 2009, cuando derrotaron a los Philadelphia Phillies.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox fans rejoice as Yankees respond to growing drama with the same Aaron Boone mistake
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The New York Yankees on October 19 confirmed something baseball fans everywhere expected. Aaron Boone will return as the Yankees' manager in 2027. Many Yankees fans are unimpressed with the decision, which means Boston Red Sox fans are celebrating it. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees on October 19 confirmed something baseball fans everywhere expected. Aaron Boone will return as the Yankees' manager in 2027. Many Yankees fans are unimpressed with the decision, which means Boston Red Sox fans are celebrating it.
If Boone was going to be fired, it probably would've happened shortly after the Tampa Bay Rays' ALDS sweep of New York. Though, Boone actually managed the series quite well, and there isn't much he could've done about the Yankees' .431 team OPS and .125 batting average with runners in scoring position.
Boone has been the skipper in the Bronx since 2018. They've made the playoffs in all but one season since then, made the World Series once but have no titles to show for their efforts. For the "27 rings" Yankees, that's a long drought. Though it wasn't started by Boone, his past managerial efforts haven't helped.
The 2027 season is the final one on Boone's contract. The Yankees haven't offered him an extension, so they could be ready to move on next year. They might be wise to hold onto Boone — the manager options available this year aren't the most inspiring, and some reporters, including Jon Heyman of the New York Post, believe that New York could be the next team to hire Alex Cora. The longtime Red Sox manager is taking the 2027 season off and the Yankees could be waiting out Boone's contract to land a highly coveted skipper next year, which would be a gut punch to Sox fans.
Red Sox fans laugh as Yankees confirm Aaron Boone's return as manager amid organizational culture drama
As Yankees fans debated the degree of fault than can be placed on Boone for the team's playoff struggles in recent years, former Yankees players have taken the conversation in a different direction. They've largely had nothing but praise for Boone, but critiqued the larger culture of the organization.
CC Sabathia has said the Yankees' "standard" hasn't been upheld — whatever that means. Nick Swisher believes the players in the locker room need to take accountability, form a bond and get it together. Alex Rodriguez said the front office needs a "philosophy change." Even David Ortiz has made comments about the degradation of the Yankees' culture and attitude from the late 90s and early 2000s. Yet, none of the issues are Boone's fault (at least, not his alone) and he's been a great manager in their eyes.
Regardless of what's wrong with the Yankees and who's to blame for their mediocrity, Red Sox fans are happy they're seemingly uninterested in figuring it out. Boone and Brian Cashman remain for at least one more season and that probably means New York's season will end the way it always has under their watch — without a title.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees 'balance and lengthen' lineup with this 1 offseason move originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees fell short in the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Very short.
Their offense managed just five runs and 12 total hits in the three-game sweep. Ben Rice showed the most fight, finishing with eight hits and four home runs in the postseason.
The Yankees are too left-handed heavy, and Aaron Judge could use a right-handed running mate in the lineup, FanSided's Zachary Rotman wrote.
"The Yankees are stacked with lefties like Rice, Cody Bellinger, Luis Garcia Jr. and Spencer Jones, but who is their best right-handed hitter not named Aaron Judge? George Lombard Jr.?
"That isn't good enough, and makes the Yankees far too easy to pitch to. Adding a big right-handed bat would help balance and lengthen the lineup, making a Yankees team with an elite pitching staff much more difficult to overtake in October," Rotman wrote.
Who might that extra right-handed hitter be? Chicago Cubs corner outfielder Seiya Suzuki is one possibility, but New York's outfield is a little crowded, even with the departure of Trent Grisham.
They could also look to add a new third baseman as an offensive upgrade over Ryan McMahon.
Alec Bohm is set to hit the open market after 15 home runs and a .698 OPS with the Philadelphia Phillies in 2026.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] 2 Astros the Yankees should target in a trade, 1 they should ignore as rumors spike
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: The New York Yankees need some type of shakeup after getting swept in the ALDS by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays. They should operate like the Yankees of old, where they were stacking their team every year and going hard for a World Series title. As a result of a weak free agency class on the offensive side, t
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees need some type of shakeup after getting swept in the ALDS by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays. The likelihood is that GM Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone aren't going anywhere. But the Yankees shouldn't just run back the same roster and hope Aaron Judge stays healthy in 2027. They should operate like the Yankees of old, where they were stacking their team every year and going hard for a World Series title.
As a result of a weak free agency class on the offensive side, the Yankees should explore the trade market in order to upgrade their lineup. They could look to the Houston Astros, who have some attractive trade pieces in their infield. For that, we're going to look at two Astros the Yankees should target via trade and one they should stay away from.
A trade the Yankees must make with the Houston Astros
Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena could be on his way out of Houston after the two sides failed to reach an agreement on a contract extension. Pena will be a free agent after next season and the Astros should trade him if they aren't going to retain the homegrown shortstop.
The Yankees are the perfect fit for Pena, who would instantly boost their offense. A trade for Pena would probably start with George Lombard Jr. However, the Yankees have the money to keep Pena for the long-term, and a lineup centered around Judge, Pena, Ben Rice, Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. could contend for a World Series title. Pena, if available, should be the Yankees' top trade target this offseason.
A Yankees fallback option
If the Yankees can't land Pena, they should pivot to Astros third baseman Isaac Paredes. The Yankees have a major hole at third base and the position has been an issue for several years. Paredes has a $13.35 million club option for 2027, which Houston will likely pick up. That salary amount is more than affordable for a trade partner to take on, including the Yankees. Paredes is coming off a big season, where he hit 25 home runs, drove in 94 RBI, had an .806 OPS and posted a 4.0 bWAR in 155 games. The Yankees shouldn't give up a Lombard or Spencer Jones for Paredes, but they have other pieces that could get a deal done, specifically their young pitching depth. Even one season of Paredes would be a significant upgrade over Ryan McMahon at third base.
An Astros trade target the Yankees should stay far away from
First baseman Christian Walker is another infielder the Astros could trade in the offseason. Walker has one more year on his deal for $20 million in 2027, and Houston's new GM could look to shed that salary. Walker was once viewed as a fit for the Yankees in recent years, but that's no longer the case. The first baseman is turning 36 years old next season and comes along with an expensive price tag for a player, who has posted a sub-.300 on-base percentage and combined 2.3 bWAR across the past two seasons. Walker does have power at the plate and brings strong defense at the first base position. That being said, the Yankees already have Garcia and Rice to man first base. Acquiring Walker at this point in time wouldn't make much sense for the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
Earlier this month, the New York Yankees got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
They lost the final game by a score of 4-3 (on their home field) in the Bronx.
A-Rod Was Wrong About The New York Yankees
One person who had been high on the Yankees was franchise legend Alex Rodriguez.
He predicted they would make the 2026 World Series (and win).
Rodriguez (via FOX Sports on October 3): “I’m going to go with the Yankees beating the Dodgers in a rematch from a couple years ago. The best two pitching staffs in the game. I’m going to go with them. Pitching and defense.”
While Yankees fans will likely enjoy knowing that Rodriguez thought they would win the title, he was obviously way off in his prediction.
Looking At The Yankees 2026 Season
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks back to the dugout after a pitching change against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning in game one of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 03, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
The Yankees had another strong regular season, finishing with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
They were the second-place team in the American League East.
In addition, the Yankees also swept the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series.
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees high fives Jose Caballero #72 prior to game one of the American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on September 29, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
The Yankees made the World Series in 2024.
However, they have still been unable to win a title since the 2009 season when they still had Rodriguez (and Derek Jeter) on the roster.
Looking At Rodriguez
Alex Rodriguez #13 of the New York Yankees looks on from second base in the first inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on August 12, 2016 in New York City.
Rodriguez was the first pick in the 1993 MLB Draft out of high school.
He spent the first 10 seasons of his career with the Seattle Mariners and Texas Rangers.
The Yankees acquired Rodriguez in a blockbuster trade with Texas in 2004.
Over 22 seasons, he won three MVP Awards (and made 14 All-Star Games).

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] CC Sabathia Reveals Who He's Pulling For In World Series
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers will play the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, with both teams looking to win the first World Series in franchise history. With all of the talk about a lockout, a salary cap and payrolls, it seems fitting that two small-market teams that don't spend a ton are in the Fall Classic. Even though the series isn't superstar-packed like a Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees matchup would have been, it should still be a very entertaining series. Both teams play a similar st
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers will play the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, with both teams looking to win the first World Series in franchise history.
With all of the talk about a lockout, a salary cap and payrolls, it seems fitting that two small-market teams that don't spend a ton are in the Fall Classic. Even though the series isn't superstar-packed like a Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees matchup would have been, it should still be a very entertaining series.
Both teams play a similar style of baseball and boast incredible pitching staffs. It really is anyone's series to win, and CC Sabathia is pulling for his former team.
"Let's go Brew Crew!!!," Sabathia posted on X after the Rays won Game 6. "It's time."
Sabathia has attended a postseason game for the Brewers this year, and even though his time on the team was brief, he is loved in Milwaukee.
He was inducted into the Brewers Wall of Honor in 2026 despite spending less than a full season with the team. However, he did help end a long postseason drought and even pitched on short rest in a contract year.
The Brewers have been knocking on the door of a championship for years, and will finally get the chance to play for one. It's no surprise Sabathia is pulling for the Brewers. Not only did he play for them, but the Rays are a rival of the New York Yankees, the team he spent most of his career with.
More MLB: Freddy Peralta Reveals Thoughts On Facing Brewers In World Series After They Traded Him

item.title: [Yardbarker] Yankees reporter reveals 'real reason' Hal Steinbrenner is running it back with Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman
item.dc:creator: Zac Wassink

item.content:encoded:
Shortly after the New York Yankees were eliminated from the playoffs by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Divisional Series round of the postseason tournament, it was reported that Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner had decided to retain team senior vice president/general manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone.
Monday reports confirmed that Boone, who is signed through the 2027 campaign, will remain the Yankees' skipper through the uncertain MLB offseason. Jon Heyman of the New York Post later noted that "it’s surely only a matter of time before we hear" that Cashman has inked a new deal with the Yankees.
For a piece published on Tuesday, Bob Klapisch of NJ Advance Media explained why Steinbrenner signed off on moves that are unpopular among pockets of Yankees fans.
"The coming labor dispute, which could be the longest and most contentious in the sport's history, is a factor in Steinbrenner's thinking," Klapisch wrote. "The season's start will almost certainly be delayed. The question is how long the owners and the [MLB Players Association] will hold out on the salary cap issue. The worst scenario says it'll be July — or just around the All-Star break — before both parties decide they've suffered enough. But that would leave a new Yankees manager in limbo for nearly nine months. Under MLB rules, a lockout halts all business and communication between team personnel — including managers, coaches, executives, and medical/training staff — and players covered by the lockout. It would be unfair, not to mention impractical, for Boone's potential replacement to hastily pull together the moving parts after a settlement."
While Boone is popular among key Yankees players such as slugger and team captain Aaron Judge, members of the franchise's fan base have spent years campaigning for Steinbrenner to make a change. Boone failed to guide the Yankees to a single World Series appearance from 2018 through the 2023 season. The Los Angeles Dodgers then needed just five games to bounce Boone's Yankees from the 2024 World Series, and the Bronx Bombers have since come up short of trips to the AL Championship Series in back-to-back years.
"October is all that matters," Klapisch added about Boone's future with the Yankees. "This was the verdict: The Yankees were booed off the field after the season-ending Game 3 loss to the Rays. Chants of 'Fire Boone!' thundered throughout the Stadium. The atmosphere has never been this hostile towards the manager. It's unlikely the anti-Boone fever will cool over the next few months. The movement will be dormant, but a new season — whenever it begins — will bring fresh calls for change."
Judge has challenged Steinbrenner and Cashman to "go all-in and do what they need to do" this offseason to give Boone a roster capable of winning the World Series. While it's unclear what such moves may look like before the expected work stoppage begins in early December, it sounds like Boone may have to guide the 2027 Yankees beyond the ALCS to remain the club's manager through the start of the 2028 campaign.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees Birthday of the Day: Mickey Mantle
item.dc:creator: Andrés Chávez
item.description: Aura. Charisma. Whatever it was, Mickey Mantle had it. Anyone can put up numbers, but no one looked as good in the process of doing it as The Mick. He was so much better than his peers that not even osteomyelitis in his left shin and a rough ACL injury in his rookie season, not to mention a myriad of other health and personal issues, could stop him from becoming the best switch-hitter who has ever stepped foot on a baseball field. Mickey Charles Mantle Born: October 20, 1931 (Spavinaw, OK) Died:
item.content:encoded:
Aura. Charisma. Whatever it was, Mickey Mantle had it. Anyone can put up numbers, but no one looked as good in the process of doing it as The Mick.
He was so much better than his peers that not even osteomyelitis in his left shin and a rough ACL injury in his rookie season, not to mention a myriad of other health and personal issues, could stop him from becoming the best switch-hitter who has ever stepped foot on a baseball field.
Mickey Charles Mantle
Born: October 20, 1931 (Spavinaw, OK)
Died: August 13, 1995 (Dallas, TX)
Yankees Tenure: 1951-68
Named after Hall of Fame catcher Mickey Cochrane, Mickey Charles Mantle was born in Spavinaw, Oklahoma, on October 20, 1931. He was the son of Elvin Charles “Mutt” Mantle and Lovell Thelma (née Richardson; previously Davis). He grew up in Commerce, Oklahoma, where he moved with his family when he was just four years old.
His father, a tough man, was a miner but also a former semi-pro baseball player. When Mantle was sent down to the minors in his rookie season and threatened to leave baseball because he thought he couldn’t compete, old Mutt told him: “I thought I raised a man. I see I raised a coward instead. You can come back to Oklahoma and work the mines with me.” That was a wake-up call for Mantle, who caught fire and never looked back.
You could say that Mutt raised Mickey to be a baseball player and, specifically, a switch-hitter. His childhood and adolescence went by playing baseball in the sandlots and hitting off his father and grandfather, but Mantle was also a multi-sport star at Commerce High School, where he excelled at football and basketball.
After penicillin saved his leg from amputation as a teenager, he gave up football and focused on baseball. Yankees scout Tom Greenwade offered the 16-year-old phenom the chance to sign for the Bombers, but he had to wait until he graduated high school a year later. He joined the Yanks’ Class D team in Independence, Kansas, and had a brilliant minor league debut in 1949. After the season ended and he went back to Oklahoma to work on the lead and zinc mines with his father, Mantle met Merlyn, a high school senior, who would later be his wife.
Even though he didn’t make his MLB debut until 1951, the Yankees called Mantle up in September of 1950. He got to witness what it was like to be a major leaguer from up close, traveling with the squad and even taking batting practice with stars such as Joe DiMaggio and Yogi Berra, among many others.
After enduring his early-1951 slump and coming back to the majors that year, Mantle hadn’t hit his ceiling yet, but the world saw glimpses of what he would eventually become: the person in charge of carrying the torch after DiMaggio. Those were some big shoes to fill.
No, Mantle wasn’t as classy as the ‘Yankee Clipper’, but he was a better player and a charismatic leader in his own way. Perhaps more importantly, he took the Yanks to a whopping seven World Series titles. The first one would come in that 1951 campaign, when he blew out his knee in Game 2 while giving DiMaggio room to make a play.
That knee injury would shape everything that was to come, but Mantle of course found a way to excel, even with a bad knee. From 1952 to 1965, Mantle made the All-Star Game every year. He added two more Midsummer Classics to his resume in 1967 and 1968. His most impressive individual achievements, however, were the three AL MVP Awards he won in 1956, 1957, and 1962.
Mantle was one of the very few ballplayers who notched at least one 200-wRC+ season and one 10-fWAR campaign. He had two of the former and three of the latter.
Mantle’s true peak was between 1956 and 1962, when he slashed a mind-blowing .316/.448/.617 with 283 home runs and a 186 wRC+. The Yankees won four World Series over that span: 1956, 1958, 1961, and 1962. Oh, and he took home the 1956 Triple Crown in the American League.
Additionally, Mantle gave us a memorable home run record chase together with his teammate and friend Roger Maris. A severe septic infection on his hip resulting from a shot he took to improve multiple health conditions knocked him out of action in September, though, giving Maris the crown and the record. Mantle still finished with 54 round-trippers, a career high.
His playing career continued until 1968, when he hit a rather disappointing .237, but with 18 homers and an excellent .385 OBP that gave him the foundation for a still-impressive 145 wRC+. Even in his last campaign as a major leaguer, he was an elite offensive performer.
Mantle retired with a .298/.421/.557 line, 536 home runs, 153 stolen bases, 1,509 RBI, and 2,415 hits. Those who watched him in his early years say he could have stolen many more bases if it weren’t for the two major leg injuries he suffered.
Mantle was a 20-time All-Star, a seven-time World Series champ, a three-time AL MVP, a Gold Glover in 1962, a batting champion in 1956, led the junior circuit in homers four times and in RBI in 1956. His number 7 is deservedly retired by the Yankees, and he has been a member of the National Baseball Hall of Fame since 1974. You can say with confidence that Mantle is one of the best players ever to play the game, and you can argue he might’ve finished even closer to the top of the list if it weren’t for injuries.
According to the Society for American Baseball Research, “Mantle struggled to find a new career after retiring from baseball. He served as a Yankee first-base coach in 1970, but abandoned that rather quickly. He invested in a hotel and a restaurant chain, both of which eventually failed. In 1983, he was given a job in public relations with the Claridge Hotel and Casino in Atlantic City.” The booming baseball memorabilia industry gave his finances some much-needed life in the eighties.
Unfortunately, he had to fight some demons during his life. He told family members and friends that he suffered from sexual abuse by his sister, Anna Bae, when he was a child. He had severe drinking problems, which eventually resulted in him being diagnosed with hepatitis and cirrhosis of the liver. It took him nearly his entire life to get sober, and shortly afterward, he was sadly diagnosed with liver cancer. “The Commerce Comet” passed away in August 1995, and the Yankees wore black armbands and a No. 7 on their sleeve to commemorate their fallen legend for the rest of the season.
Mantle is, simply put, one of the greatest Yankees of all time. Maybe he wasn’t always a role model, but boy, could he play the game.

item.title: [Fox News] Aaron Boone will return for 10th season as Yankees manager despite fan outrage: reports
item.dc:creator: Ryan Morik
item.description: The New York Yankees are running it back again. After yet another season of another team celebrating on their own field, reports say Aaron Boone will return for his 10th season as the team's manager. Boone's contract expires after the 2027 season, and assuming the owners lock out the players on Dec. 1, managers are not allowed to communicate with players. So, perhaps management is not willing to take the risk of losing a manager who has finished over .500 in each season and made the postseason i
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are running it back again.
After yet another season of another team celebrating on their own field, reports say Aaron Boone will return for his 10th season as the team's manager.
Boone's contract expires after the 2027 season, and assuming the owners lock out the players on Dec. 1, managers are not allowed to communicate with players. So, perhaps management is not willing to take the risk of losing a manager who has finished over .500 in each season and made the postseason in eight of his nine campaigns.
However, the fan base has grown incensed, as Boone is the only manager in team history to hold his post for at least five seasons and not win a title.
The Yankees' 2026 season was almost a carbon copy of last season, going 93-68 and getting swept in the American League Division Series by the eventual pennant-winning Tampa Bay Rays, their own division rival. In 2025, they went 94-68 and lost to their division rival, the Toronto Blue Jays, in the ALDS, who were inches away from winning the World Series.
Reports circulated that owner Hal Steinbrenner had been aware of the fans' disdain for their manager - chants of "Fire Boone" rang through Yankee Stadium as the Yankees' season ended.
Boone was hired after the Yankees opted not to bring back Joe Girardi following the 2017 season. He was given a four-year deal and then extended another four years. After the 2024 season, in which they lost the World Series, Boone was given a second extension, which is his current deal.
A common criticism of Boone is that he is not harsh enough on his players, which leads to lazy play and mental mistakes during a "June Swoon," which the Yankees seem to take forever to crawl out of. Under Boone, the Yankees have won the division three times and the pennant once, yet they've beaten only one team in a postseason series that had a better record than they did (2020 Wild Card Series vs. Cleveland).
The Seattle Mariners and Houston Astros are the only teams that are looking for managers after letting go of Dan Wilson and Joe Espada, respectively. The New York Mets (Andy Green), Boston Red Sox (Chad Tracy) and Philadelphia Phillies (Don Mattingly) have all retained their interim managers on a full-time basis.

item.content:encoded:
Los Yankees de Nueva York vuelven a la carga.
Tras otra temporada más en la que otro equipo ha celebrado la victoria en su propio campo, según las noticias, Aaron Boone volverá para su décima temporada como entrenador del equipo.
El contrato de Boone vence al final de la temporada 2027 y, si los propietarios declaran el cierre patronal el 1 de diciembre, los entrenadores no podrán comunicarse con los jugadores. Así que, quizá la directiva no esté dispuesta a arriesgarse a perder a un entrenador que ha terminado cada temporada con un balance por encima de .500 y ha llegado a la postemporada en ocho de sus nueve temporadas.
Sin embargo, la afición está furiosa, ya que Boone es el único entrenador en la historia del equipo que ha estado en el cargo al menos cinco temporadas sin ganar ningún título.
La temporada 2026 de los Yankees fue casi una copia exacta de la anterior: acabaron con un balance de 93-68 y fueron barridos en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana por los Tampa Bay Rays, que a la postre se llevaron el título de la liga y que son sus rivales de división. En 2025, acabaron con un balance de 94-68 y perdieron en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana ante sus rivales de división, los Toronto Blue Jays, que estuvieron a un pelo de ganar la Serie Mundial.
Se rumoreaba que el propietario, Hal Steinbrenner, ya sabía del rechazo de los aficionados hacia su entrenador: al final de la temporada de los Yankees, el Yankee Stadium retumbaba con cánticos de «Fuera Boone».
Boone fue contratado después de que los Yankees decidieran no renovar al Joe e Girardi tras la temporada de 2017. Le ofrecieron un contrato de cuatro años que luego se prorrogó otros cuatro. Tras la temporada de 2024, en la que perdieron la Serie Mundial, a Boone le concedieron una segunda prórroga, que es su contrato actual.
Una crítica habitual a Boone es que no es lo bastante duro con sus jugadores, lo que lleva a un juego flojo y a errores mentales durante el «bajón de junio», del que a los Yankees parece que les cuesta una eternidad salir. Bajo el mando de Boone, los Yankees han ganado la división tres veces y el título de liga una vez, pero solo han vencido a un equipo en una serie de postemporada que tuviera mejor balance que ellos (la serie de comodín de 2020 contra Cleveland).
Los Seattle Mariners y los Houston Astros son los únicos equipos que están buscando entrenadores tras despedir a Dan Wilson y Joe Espada, respectivamente. Los New York Mets (Andy Green), los Boston Red Sox (Chad Tracy) y los Philadelphia Phillies (Don Mattingly) han confirmado a sus entrenadores interinos de forma permanente.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Aaron Boone's lame duck return to Yankees has an MLB lockout excuse that doesn't hold water
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: The New York Yankees are bringing Aaron Boone back for 2027, as expected, and won't be giving him an extension, as expected. Somehow, the Bombers managed to annoy everyone. Boone haters are bummed out that he's returning and the Yankees can't figure out when to pull the plug, and Boone backers are bothered the team won't really stand behind him. The Yankees value continuity and sending people out with whispers, not bombast. If Boone doesn't win the World Series in '27, expect his contract to sim
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are bringing Aaron Boone back for 2027, as expected, and won't be giving him an extension, as expected. Somehow, the Bombers managed to annoy everyone. Boone haters are bummed out that he's returning and the Yankees can't figure out when to pull the plug, and Boone backers are bothered the team won't really stand behind him.
The Yankees value continuity and sending people out with whispers, not bombast. If Boone doesn't win the World Series in '27, expect his contract to simply expire. But the added wrinkle to this conversation is the looming MLB lockout, which - to be fair - does make it extremely difficult to add a new manager to the mix. There's a reason the Phillies chose to run it back with Don Mattingly, while the Mariners and Astros remain the only current teams with vacancies.
If the Yankees were to bring in a new manager, there'd be no contact with players post-Dec. 1 until the end of the lockout. Looking to instill a new culture? Well, that could be difficult when you can't meet anybody. The Yankees are going to have to try to shift their philosophy with new voices, potentially hitting coach and bench coach changes. That's going to be difficult enough. We get it.
But, as MLB insider Robert Murray said on The Baseball Insiders last week, he thinks the Yankees might've responded to the noise differently without the reality of the looming lockout. And that sets up a very difficult 2027 reality.
"When guys like Joe Girardi and CC Sabathia, who have deep ties to the organization [speak out], that speaks volumes. It increases the pressure on [Boone and Cashman]," Murray said on last Wednesday's show. "I don't think this year is going to be the year for those changes, but next year, when we don't have a lockout looming over our heads, I think the answer could be different. If we didn't have a lockout now, I think my answer also would've changed here as well. I think we could've seen a change at manager. I think we might be at that point."
MLB lockout changing Yankees' Aaron Boone plans makes sense ... but also reveals an unfortunate answer
If true, that would mean ... the Yankees have already made the opposite decision on Boone, or are at least open to the conversation of a change. But, for multiple reasons, the lockout included, they've decided to move forward with a manager they might think is inadequate, partially because the logistics don't match.
The lockout does complicate this significantly. It also gives the Yankees a ready-made excuse. If the decision would be different in a vacuum, it should probably be different in reality, too. If he's not the guy, he's not the guy.
The '27 Yankees used to be the stand-in for "baseball excellence". Now, that terminology might be redefined as "the year the Yankees chose to move on from their manager, but didn't on a technicality". There may be no better metaphor for the degrading of the Yankees brand than that. From Murderers' Row to murdering a season before it begins.

item.title: [Kings of Kauffman] Yankees trade rumors could put an affordable arm on the Royals' radar
item.dc:creator: Matthew Swigonski

New York Yankees pitcher Luis Gil has taken quite a tumble over the past few seasons. item.content:encoded:
As one former AL Rookie of the Year is currently stuck in baseball limbo, the Kansas City Royals could take a bold chance to bolster their depleted pitching staff. New York Yankees pitcher Luis Gil has taken quite a tumble over the past few seasons. He went from one of the best and brightest young pitchers in the game to essentially a throwaway player without a role in New York.
While Gil has recently seen his fair share of struggles, he could become an ideal candidate as a reclamation project for the Royals. The 28-year-old pitcher has thrown just over 84 innings since being named as the top Rookie in the AL in 2024. As a result, he's continued to become buried on the team's depth chart. Now the Yankees will have to make a choice regarding his future very shortly.
According to Joel Sherman of the New York Post, Gil may be non-tendered in November since he is projected to make a little over $2 million in 2027. In an entry into his Pinstripe Post podcast series, Sherman speculated that the Yankees could be willing to part ways with a pitcher that they once held in high regard in order to save that money and spend it elsewhere.
Since Gil will no longer have any minor league options left next season, the Yankees will be very limited in what they can do with him still on the payroll. Thanks to a crowded pitching staff and a number of young arms waiting in the wings, this means that Gil could become expendable for the Bronx Bombers. This creates an interesting opportunity for the Royals.
Luis Gil could give the Royals a dynamic arm on their pitching staff
Unlike the Yankees, who are seemingly blessed with an endless parade of viable arms, the Royals are in desperate need for pitching depth. After a brutal rash of injuries ripped through the pitching staff in Kansas City in 2026, the team struggled to keep their head above water. Those injuries could continue to have a rippling effect well into next season.
Pitchers Cole Ragans, Stephen Kolek, and Luinder Avila all had season-ending surgeries in 2026 and will have a challenging road ahead of them if they are set to return at some point next year. That means that there will be a number of holes to fill throughout the Royals’ pitching staff. Royals GM J.J. Picollo will likely look to free agency to add some affordable arms, but he could look to the Yankees and Gil as another viable option.
Outside of the affordable $2.3 million contract that Gil is set to earn in 2027, he likely wouldn’t cost the Royals a fortune in prospects to acquire either. Without a clear future on the Yankees and limited production over the last two seasons, Gil is now at a diminished trade value that lands squarely inside the Royals’ budget. Even with boom or bust potential, it just might be worth the risk.
In his 20 appearances since 2024, Gil has seen a substantial regression across the board. His walks per nine rate still remains well above 4.5 while his strikeout rate has nearly been slashed in half. Gil has struck out just 58 batters in 84.1 innings of work during that time frame. This was due in part to his lack of control and a drop in velocity over the last two years. Simply put, Gil has no longer been able to get opponents to swing and miss.
Okay, you might read that and think that the Royals would be foolish to even consider dealing for a pitcher who appears to have completely lost his "It" factor. But Gil has dealt with numerous injuries of his own since 2024. From shoulder inflammation to a lat strain, Gil has not been able to stay on the mound long enough to recapture his dominant form. But with a clean bill of health and a full offseason to get back on track, there is optimism that Gil can get back to becoming a successful pitcher in the big leagues.
As a buy-low option for the 2027 season, Gil could be a worthwhile risk for the Royals. If he pitches well enough to help the team get back to postseason contention, he'll be considered a steal. If he pitches poorly and is designated for assignment by June, nobody would blame the Royals' front office for trying. They don't really have much to lose.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have watched catcher Austin Wells spiral at the plate throughout his 2026 campaign.
While he’s been productive on defense, his offensive ability dropped early on.
During the second half of the season, he showed improvements, but red flags are still raised.
To combat this, the Atlanta Braves could have what the Yankees need.
Yankees Could Trade McMahon for Braves’ Catcher
Stephen Parello of FanSided recently proposed a risky yet interesting New York-Atlanta trade involving 31-year-old infielder Ryan McMahon.
If the Yankees were to ship him out, he suggested a return package consisting of catcher Sean Murphy and low-level prospects.
“As we know, McMahon has one year and $16 million left on his deal, while Atlanta Braves catcher Sean Murphy is owed $30 million over the next two seasons,” he wrote. “That imbalance should net the Yankees a lottery ticket prospect or two.”
He added, “It’s a gamble, but with New York expected to keep Austin Wells as the starter, Murphy could be the highest-upside right-handed-hitting complement the club can find.”
As Parello pointed out, Murphy comes with an injury-riddled history, and he’s in his age-32 season.
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 03: Sean Murphy #12 of the Atlanta Braves celebrates after hitting a solo home run in the sixth inning against the Los Angeles Dodgers in game one of the National League Division Series at Dodger Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images)
During his latest campaign, he slashed .182/.256/.300 with a .556 OPS and three homers through 33 games.
In 2025, he appeared in 94 games and slashed .199/.300/.409 with a .709 OPS and 16 home runs.
Along the way, he registered 13 doubles and 45 RBIs.
He certainly doesn’t come with a glowing stat sheet, but if he’s packaged with a couple of prospects, perhaps New York would bite.
Nonetheless, it’s a risky proposal.
Yankees Approach Long, Grueling Hot Stove Season
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – SEPTEMBER 30: Ryan McMahon #19 of the New York Yankees throws to first base after a ground ball hit by Adley Rutschman #31 of the Boston Red Sox during the third inning in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
As soon as the postseason ends, hot stove season, well, heats up.
McMahon is floating in numerous trade rumors right now — this is only one of many.
On Oct. 14, Brendan Kuty of The Athletic wrote, “Known mostly for his glove, McMahon turned in his worst defensive season by far, posting minus-3 Defensive Runs Saved. He was still capable of making brilliant plays, but he struggled too often with routine plays, and he didn’t appear to go side-to-side as well as he did in the past.
He’s also been terrible offensively since joining the Yankees at the 2025 trade deadline, posting a 78 wRC+, the 39th-ranked mark among MLB third basemen with at least 350 plate appearances during that span.”
This was far from an impressive season for McMahon, which is in large part why he’s stuck in trade talk.
It’s time for New York to ship him out — the Braves could be a suitor.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees could target Brewers All-Star if David Bednar leaves in free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees' bullpen may look totally different in 2027.
Six of their relievers will soon become free agents, including closer David Bednar.
The Yankees can extend him a qualifying offer, which would bring him back to New York for at least one season if he accepts.
Bednar is one of the more consistent closers in baseball, converting 35 of 39 saves this season. It would be a major loss for the Yankees if he decides to sign with another club.
Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote that this will be a huge offseason for New York's bullpen roster construction.
"With David Bednar and darn near every other reliever of note hitting free agency, the Yankees have quite a bit of work to do on their bullpen. The dream target would be Mason Miller, if the Padres are willing to have that conversation," Miller wrote.
He identified Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill as someone the Yankees should target if they fail to re-sign Bednar.
"But while trading for Devin Williams didn't pan out how they hoped in 2025, going back to Milwaukee for Trevor Megill could be the move. He was an All-Star last year and probably ought to be a three-time reigning All-Star at this point," Miller added.
Megill throws a power fastball and nasty knuckle curve, which helped him punch out 69 batters in 61.2 innings in 2026.
He reaches free agency in 2028, and the Brewers have a history of trading their stars one year before they hit the open market.
Josh Hader and Devin Williams (both traded) were in identical contract situations as Megill.

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — The price of a qualifying offer for this year’s major league free agents rose 5.1% to $23.15 million from $22,025,000.
The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year. The price dropped by $100,000 to $17.8 million in 2019, then rose to $18.9 million in 2020, fell $500,000 in 2021 and rose to $19.65 million in 2022, $20,325,000 in 2023 and $21.05 million in 2024.
Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 offers have been accepted.
A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he has been with the same team continuously since opening day and has never received a qualifying offer before.
Among the top players who can become free agents after the World Series and are eligible to receive qualifying offers are Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena, New York Yankees left-hander David Bednar, Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon, Baltimore left-hander Trevor Roger and Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki.
A record four players accepted last year from among the 13 who received offers: Chicago Cubs left-hander Shota Imanaga, Milwaukee right-hander Brandon Woodruff, New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham and Detroit second baseman Gleyber Torres.
Other potential free agents ineligible for qualifying offers this offseason include Philadelphia second baseman Luis Arraez, Baltimore right-hander Chris Bassitt, New York Mets third baseman Bo Bichette, Arizona right-hander Zac Gallen, San Diego right-hander Michael King, Padres left-hander Robbie Ray, Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Tarik Skubal and Toronto outfielder George Springer.
Bichette and King must decide on player options.
A qualifying offer can be made through the fifth day after the World Series, and a player has a week after that to accept.
If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the amateur draft, his former club would receive a draft pick as compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.
Qualifying offers began at $13.3 million. Other players who accepted are Baltimore catcher Matt Wieters, Houston outfielder Colby Rasmus and Dodgers left-hander Brett Anderson ($15.8 million for 2016); Mets second baseman Neil Walker and Philadelphia right-hander Jeremy Hellickson ($17.2 million for 2017); Dodgers left-hander Hyun Jin Ryu ($17.9 million for 2019); Chicago White Sox first baseman José Abreu and Minnesota right-hander Jake Odorizzi ($17.8 million for 2020); San Francisco right-hander Kevin Gausman and Mets right-hander Marcus Stroman ($18.9 million for 2021); Giants first baseman Brandon Belt ($18.4 million for 2022; Texas left-hander Martín Pérez and Giants outfielder Joc Pederson ($19.65 million for 2023); and Cincinnati Reds right-hander Nick Martinez ($21.05 million for 2025).

item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone will return as manager of the New York Yankees in 2027, the Bergen Record reports. Next season is the final season on Boone's contract and will be his 10th season as Yankees manager. New York is 790-565 (.583) in nine seasons under Boone. The Yankees have reached the postseason eight times in those nine seasons but have not won the World Series.
"That's for another day," Boone said when asked about his job status after the Yankees were swept by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. "Right now is about trying to reflect on this, trying to connect with guys right now as much as I can. Appreciative of a lot of things, but those conversations and things are for another day."
Unless the Yankees give Boone a contract extension, he will enter next season as a lame duck, and that season could come with a World Series or bust mandate. The Yankees have had only three managers in the last 30 years: Joe Torre from 1996-2007, Joe Girardi from 2008-17, and Boone since 2018. Torre and Girardi both won the World Series within their first two seasons.
Why the Yankees are sticking with Boone
The Yankees have not fired a manager who was under contract since Stump Merrill after the 1991 season (Torre and Girardi were let go after their contracts expired). Hal Steinbrenner is much more patient than his father, perhaps to his detriment, but Steinbrenner and GM Brian Cashman are supportive of Boone. That all made Boone's return more likely than not.
Furthermore, this is a bad offseason to need a new manager. Team personnel, including managers, can not communicate with players during a lockout, which is considered likely when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. Relationship-building with players is most of the job, and it will be difficult for a new manager to foster those during the lockout.
Only the Los Angeles Dodgers have won more games than the Yankees since Boone was named manager in 2018. This is a franchise that is judged on championships, however, and New York has not won a World Series since 2009. The Yankees have won just one pennant since then (2024), and their 17-year title drought is tied for the longest in franchise history with their 1979-95 stretch.
Aaron Boone as Yankees manager
| Season | Record | Playoffs |
| 2018 | 100-62 | Lost ALDS |
| 2019 | 103-59 | Lost ALCS |
| 2020 | 33-27 | Lost ALDS |
| 2021 | 92-70 | Lost AL Wild Card |
| 2022 | 99-63 | Lost ALCS |
| 2023 | 82-80 | N/A |
| 2024 | 94-68 | Lost World Series |
| 2025 | 94-68 | Lost ALDS |
| 2026 | 93-68 | Lost ALDS |
Cashman is currently without a contract, though he is expected to return for what would be his 29th season as their head baseball operations executive. .
The Yankees went 93-68 in 2026. It was their 34th consecutive winning season. The Houston Astros and Seattle Mariners are the only two teams with a managerial vacancy at the moment.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Yankees make decision about Aaron Boone for 2027
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra

The offseason before a contract expires is often decision time, and no manager likes to go into the final year with limited certainty about his future. item.content:encoded:
In Major League Baseball, the length of a manager’s contract is treated more like a rough suggestion rather than a firm timeline for a man to hold a job title. The offseason before a contract expires is often decision time, and no manager likes to go into the final year with limited certainty about his future.
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone will enter the last year of his contract in 2027. For now at least, the Yankees have no plans to let him go.
Pete Caldera of the Bergen Record was the first to report on Monday, Oct. 19, that Boone will return to the bench in the Bronx next season. Whether he is offered—or signs—a long-term extension is another matter.
Boone, 53, led the Yankees to 93 wins and a second-place finish in the American League East in 2026. They defeated the Boston Red Sox in a two-game wild-card sweep and then lost to the Tampa Bay Rays in the Division Series round.
Closing in on a decade
In nine seasons as the Yankees’ manager, Boone is 790-565 (.583). Among active managers, only Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts boasts a better regular-season winning percentage. Only 15 other men have a better winning percentage in MLB history, and 10 of them are in the Hall of Fame.
Those eye-popping factoids do little to satisfy fans for whom anything less than a World Series title is seen as a failure. Whether a different manager could have piloted the Yankees on a deep postseason run without injured star Aaron Judge (who wasn’t active in October or for most of the regular season) is up for debate.
One thing is clear: The Yankees’ front office has an excellent working relationship with Boone, and neither party is eager for it to end.

item.description: The New York Yankees are sticking with Aaron Boone next season after all. After speculation that the team would move on following their latest postseason exit, Boone will return as the Yankees manager in 2027, according to USA Today's Pete Caldera and the YES Network's Jack Curry. Boone signed a two-year extension through the 2027 MLB season in Feb. 2025, months after the Yankees lost the World Series to the Los Angeles Dodgers. After two straight eliminations in the ALDS, many expected his time
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are sticking with Aaron Boone next season after all.
After speculation that the team would move on following their latest postseason exit, Boone will return as the Yankees manager in 2027, according to USA Today's Pete Caldera and the YES Network's Jack Curry.
Boone signed a two-year extension through the 2027 MLB season in Feb. 2025, months after the Yankees lost the World Series to the Los Angeles Dodgers. After two straight eliminations in the ALDS, many expected his time would be up in New York after nine seasons. Instead, Boone will now manage through the end of his current deal.
The 2026 season saw the Yankees finish second in the AL East for the second straight season and win 90 games for the seventh time over a full season under Boone. It's been the postseason where the Yankees fell short more often than not under the 53-year-old.
Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season
The Yankees hold a 27-30 playoff record under Boone, which included three trips to the ALCS and one World Series appearance. His teams were 18-5 as the higher seed in a series and 9-25 as the lower seed. The Yankees were the No. 4 seed in 2026 and beat the No. 5 seed Boston Red Sox in the wild-card round before being swept by the top-seeded Tampa Rays in the ALDS.
Without Aaron Judge and with Giancarlo Stanton only available as a pinch-hitter, the Yankees batted .130 in the ALDS, and three of their five RBI came from Ben Rice. Their pitching was what kept them in games, as evidenced by a 1.88 team ERA, 0.81 team WHIP and a .173 opponent batting average.
Other teams picked up on the weaknesses of Boone's Yankee teams. The Dodgers told their players their 2024 World Series opponents were "talent over fundamentals" and were bound to self-destruct. Toronto Blue Jays announcer Buck Martinez labeled the AL East rivals as "not a good team" last season, saying they were mistake-prone in the field and on the bases.
Those criticisms were only hardened after seeing Austin Wells' baserunner mistake in Game 1 against the Rays and then the Yankees' defensive breakdown in Game 2.
General manager Brian Cashman has been in charge for 29 seasons. Boone is just the third manager to work under him. The Yankees last won the World Series in 2009 and are in the midst of a 17-year championship drought. The boos heard after Trent Grisham's series-ending strikeout against the Rays showed how frustrated the fanbase is with the team's current state.
But regardless of their feelings, Cashman isn't ready to hire a new manager just yet. It's unclear what changes he will make this winter, if any major ones at all, in hopes of returning the franchise to contender status.

item.title: [The Times of India] Yankees all-star CC Sabathia helps fund $11 million ‘Harlem Field of Dreams’; renovated Brigadier General Charles Young Playground field now serves five sports
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
item.description: CC Sabathia, the former New York Yankees pitcher, has helped transform a dilapidated dirt field in Harlem into a place where children can play. Through his PitCCh In Foundation, Sabathia joined public agencies and sports organisations to fund the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams at Brigadier General Charles Young Playground. The renovated field now accommodates five sports, offers free youth programming, and honours a remarkable figure in American military history. Here is how the project was
item.content:encoded:
CC Sabathia, the former New York Yankees pitcher, has helped transform a dilapidated dirt field in Harlem into a place where children can play. Through his PitCCh In Foundation, Sabathia joined public agencies and sports organisations to fund the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams at Brigadier General Charles Young Playground. The renovated field now accommodates five sports, offers free youth programming, and honours a remarkable figure in American military history. Here is how the project was paid for, what the new field offers local families, and why the history of the playground and its surroundings matters to the neighbourhood.
How the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams was funded, asset forfeiture money and foundation donations
According to a 2025 press release from the Office of the Mayor of New York City, the $11 million project drew on several funding sources. Roughly $7.5 million came from law enforcement asset forfeiture funds from the New York and New Jersey High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area program, in partnership with the New York City Police Department and the New York City Police Foundation. Additional contributions came from Sabathia's PitCCh In Foundation, Major League Baseball, the Major League Baseball Players Association Youth Development Fund, the National Football League Foundation Grassroots Program, the Cal Ripken Senior Foundation, the Manhattan Borough President's Office, and the New York City Council.
The release does not say how much each partner gave, so Sabathia's exact share is not specified.
Five sports, more than 800 young players, and new amenities on the renovated Harlem athletic field
The project turned a dilapidated dirt field into a 150,000 square foot synthetic turf field built for multiple sports. Eric Adams, then mayor of New York City, told the public in the release that more than 800 young people can now play baseball, football, soccer, and lacrosse there. The city says the field accommodates five sports in total, with softball completing the list. Upgrades include improved drainage and water detention, drinking fountains, fencing, backstops, benches, dugouts, and a sports mister. The release describes a $9 million transformation, while the mayor's remarks and later sections cite $11 million for the full project. Sabathia told the public that giving back has always been at the heart of everything he does, and that New York has become his second home.
Sabathia in July 2018 (Image: Wikipedia)
Free Saturday Night Lights programming and a public safety approach that keeps young people engaged
The city plans to offer free youth sports on the new field through the New York City Department of Youth and Community Development's Saturday Night Lights program, which the release describes as a way to give young people safe places to play while building trust between law enforcement and communities. The field is part of an upstream approach to public safety that invests in free programming to keep young people engaged when they are not in school. Earlier improvements in 2023 included new asphalt and fencing for the main basketball court, repairs to three basketball courts, and the conversion of one court into a soccer pitch. The field house bathrooms are also set for upgrades with $2.5 million in public funding.
Brigadier General Charles Young, the history behind the Harlem playground and the Hellfighters armoury
The playground is named for Brigadier General Charles Young, who was born into slavery in Kentucky in 1864 and became the third Black graduate of the United States Military Academy at West Point. According to the release, he served more than 30 years in the United States Army and became the first African American colonel before being forced into medical retirement in 1917. To prove his fitness, he rode 497 miles on horseback to Washington, though his appeal failed, and he was posthumously promoted in 2022. The playground sits just north of the 369th Regiment Armoury, home to the Harlem Hellfighters, a regiment that saw more combat than any other unit during World War One. Cal Ripken Junior told the public that the field is the 125th Youth Development Park, opened by the Cal Ripken Senior Foundation.

item.dc:creator: Madison Pavich
item.description: Unfortunately, it’s time to ponder what comes next already. The Yankees were eliminated in the ALDS by their division rivals for the second straight year, and it’s safe to say that allowing that process to play out a third consecutive year would cause some nuclear-reactor level meltdowns. item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, it’s time to ponder what comes next already. The Yankees were eliminated in the ALDS by their division rivals for the second straight year, and it’s safe to say that allowing that process to play out a third consecutive year would cause some nuclear-reactor level meltdowns. The immediate aftermath of their elimination was handled by my colleague Jake in our last mailbag while the team was still active, but now that the team is officially in offseason mode it’s time to start picking apart what went wrong and what the team can do going forward.
There’s a lot of moving parts in the Yankees’ roster turnover this year, with 10 free agents to be, though there’s still a lot of money tied up to the superstars of the roster making some big swings unlikely. Still, there’s room for a sizeable makeover if Brian Cashman and company can get creative. How can the team revamp its offense after struggling to put rallies together for most of the year and when it mattered most? What will come of Aaron Judge’s lost year and his frustrations with how the team is currently looking? What bright spots can they build around from an otherwise lost year? If you have questions like these, or anything else on your mind, send ‘em in for a chance to be featured in our Yankees mailbag.
Answers will run on Friday afternoon. All questions received by the night of October 22nd will be considered. You can leave your submissions in the comment section below or by e-mail to pinstripealleyblog [at] gmail [dot] com.

item.title: [Sportsnaut] Rumor Opens Door For NY Mets to Address Major Need in Trade With NY Yankees This Winter: What Would a Deal Cost?
