item.content:encoded:
Marlins Video
Don Mattingly had the longest managerial tenure in Miami Marlins history, holding the position from 2016-22. It seemed as though that would likely be his last opportunity to serve as an MLB skipper, but then a Philadelphia Phillies team with high expectations got off to a dreadful 9-19 start this season. That's when they fired Rob Thomson and elevated Mattingly from his bench coach role to interim manager. Nearly two weeks after the Phillies were knocked out by the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card Series, they have decided to take off the interim label. signing him to a two-year contract that runs through the 2028 season.
Mattingly, 65, is second-oldest active manager in the league, trailing only Pat Murphy of the Milwaukee Brewers (67).
Certainly worth noting, the Phillies’ general manager is Mattingly’s son, Preston. Given that glaring conflict of interest, it’s safe to assume his boss, Dave Dombrowski, was the one who made the ultimate decision.
According to Bob Nightengale of USA Today, Dombrowski targeted Alex Cora as his manager twice—after Thomson was fired and again following the Phillies’ postseason elimination. Cora, who’s still being paid by his previous employer, the Boston Red Sox, has opted to sit out the 2027 season.

item.content:encoded:
Panamá/El pelotero panameño José 'Chema'Caballero es uno de los finalistas al Premio Guante de Oro 2026 del béisbol de las Grandes Ligas.
Caballero se encuentra en el grupo de tres finalistas en el puesto de utility para la Liga Americana. Este es un rol que realizan aquellos peloteros que juegan varias posiciones.
Según un informe emitido por Major League Baseball en su página web, "Caballero acumuló +12 Carreras Defensivas Salvadas (DRS) mientras se desempeñaba en distintas posiciones del terreno con los Yankees. Jugó en todas las posiciones defensivas, excepto como lanzador, receptor y primera base. Su Valor de Carreras a la Defensiva (FRV) de 0 es, de hecho, el más bajo de su carrera, después de alcanzar su mejor cifra de +8 como novato con los Marineros en el 2023. Sin embargo, Caballero es finalista al Guante de Oro por primera vez".
Esta será la quinta ocasión consecutiva en la que se otorgará un Guante de Oro para el rol de utility.
Los finalistas fueron revelados este miércoles y los ganadores se darán a conocer el domingo 1 de noviembre.
Te puede interesar: Temblor en Panamá: José 'Chema' Caballero, su familia y vicecónsul hacen donación a comunidad en Tonosí
La lista completa de los finalistas es la siguiente:
Liga Americana
Lanzador
- Tanner Bibee, Guardianes
- Jacob deGrom, Rangers
- José Soriano, Angelinos/Azulejos
Receptor
- Dillon Dingler, Tigres
- Brandon Valenzuela, Azulejos

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Brewers' Jackson Chourio Matches Derek Jeter, More With First-Pitch NLCS Blast
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers got on the board right away on Wednesday night, to say the least. Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell took the hill for the Los Angeles Dodgers and on the very first pitch of the game, Jackson Chourio struck. Chourio, who already hit one home run in the postseason entering the contest, launched his second to give the Brewers a 1-0 lead. In the process, Chourio tied Derek Jeter, Jimmy Rollins and Shohei Ohtani for the second-most postseason leadoff home runs in big le
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers got on the board right away on Wednesday night, to say the least.
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell took the hill for the Los Angeles Dodgers and on the very first pitch of the game, Jackson Chourio struck. Chourio, who already hit one home run in the postseason entering the contest, launched his second to give the Brewers a 1-0 lead.
In the process, Chourio tied Derek Jeter, Jimmy Rollins and Shohei Ohtani for the second-most postseason leadoff home runs in big league history. The only player with more is Kyle Schwarber of the Philadelphia Phillies, who has five, per MLB's Sarah Langs.
"Most postseason leadoff home runs: Kyle Schwarber: 5, Jackson Chourio: 3, Shohei Ohtani: 3, Derek Jeter: 3, Jimmy Rollins: 3," Langs wrote.
Simply absurd, especially when you take into account the fact that Chourio is just 22 years old. He's already in his third postseason for the Brewers and already has hit six total home runs in 18 games, as of the first inning on Wednesday night.
Chourio blasted a leadoff homer against the NLCS last year, also on Oct. 14. Last year, Chourio did so in Game 2.
Also, with the first-inning homer, Chourio took the lead for the most postseason home runs in Brewers history from William Contreras. Chourio has six long balls in the playoffs and Contreras has five.
We're seemingly witnessing history on a nightly basis at this point with Chourio. He's in his third season and yet the Brewers knew they had a star. They handed him a long-term extension before he even took the field for a big league game and it already looks like a steal. If he continues on the trajectory that he's on — both in the regular season and in the postseason — we'll be talking about a Brewers all-time great when all is said and done.
Chourio missed the first few weeks of the 2026 season. When he ultimately took the field, he put together the best season of his young career to this point. Chourio slashed .291/.351/.487 with an .837 OPS, 25 home runs, 75 RBIs and 23 stolen bases in 127 games played. He's been very good in the postseason as well. He hit a homer in the NLDS in Game 1 against the San Diego Padres and then had a walk-off single in Game 2. Now, he's on the board in the NLCS as well.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding "Milwaukee Brewers On SI," please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.dc:creator: Jackson Kruse
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays knocked the New York Yankees out of the postseason with a 3-0 sweep in the American League Division Series. The Yankees have now failed to win the World Series for 17 straight seasons, the second-longest streak in franchise history. Aaron Boone has been the Yankees’ manager since the 2018 season. Naturally, many are wondering if it’s time for New York to fire the long-time skipper. Former Yankees manager Joe Girardi comments on Boone’s job status on Wednesday. Joe Girardi Make
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays knocked the New York Yankees out of the postseason with a 3-0 sweep in the American League Division Series.
The Yankees have now failed to win the World Series for 17 straight seasons, the second-longest streak in franchise history.
Aaron Boone has been the Yankees’ manager since the 2018 season. Naturally, many are wondering if it’s time for New York to fire the long-time skipper.
Former Yankees manager Joe Girardi comments on Boone’s job status on Wednesday.
Joe Girardi Makes Aaron Boone Statement After Yankees’ Playoff Exit
HOUSTON, TX – OCTOBER 14: Manager Joe Girardi #28 of the New York Yankees looks on during batting practice prior to game two of the American League Championship Series against the Houston Astros at Minute Maid Park on October 14, 2017 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images)
Girardi went on a New York Post podcast with Jon Heyman and Joel Sherman.
Sherman asked Girardi if he thinks Boone has “reached his shelf life” and if a “new voice is needed.”
NEW YORK, NY – APRIL 15: Joe Girardi #28 of the New York Yankees cheers on his players prior to taking on the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on April 15, 2017 in the Bronx borough of New York City. All players are wearing #42 in honor of Jackie Robinson Day. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images)
“I don’t think [Boone’s shelf life has been reached]. Here’s why I’ll say no,” Girardi said. “I think that you could argue that this was his best year of managing. I think he got the most out of this team during the course of the season with all they had to deal with. He had to flip the way they won games.”
They had to win them from a pitching standpoint, different from some of the years past where they would win by just outslugging people,” Girardi added. “He couldn’t do that this year. I think he ran the bullpen extremely well. I think he got the most out of those guys. You think about the progress that Headrick made, what he did with Blackburn.”
“I think you could argue this was his best year. They didn’t get it done in the playoffs. One of the things that reared its ugly head a lot during the season was the offense. Can you say that that’s his fault? I don’t think so. I just don’t think the guys had the year they projected them to have, or some of the guys just aren’t as good as they thought they would be.”
Looking at Joe Girardi’s time with the Yankees
NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 04: Manager Joe Girardi #27 of the New York Yankees celebrate after their 7-3 win against the Philadelphia Phillies in Game Six of the 2009 MLB World Series at Yankee Stadium on November 4, 2009 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Pool/Getty Images)
Girardi replaced Joe Torre as the Yankees manager before the 2008 season.
The Yankees won the 2009 World Series under Girardi.
New York and Girardi parted ways after the 2017 season. He had a 910-710 regular-season record with the team.

item.content:encoded:
Last week, the New York Yankees got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
They lost the final game (in the Bronx) by a score of 4-3.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. had no hits (and one stolen base) off the bench.
New York Yankees Star Aaron Judge Was Wrong About Jazz
Chisholm Jr. had a tough season where he batted .231 with 19 home runs in 137 games.
That said, he did have 41 stolen bases.
Heading into the season, Yankees star Aaron Judge had high hopes for Chisholm Jr.
He spoke about him in an interview with Kevin Durant that was released on March 25 (via Boardroom).
Durant: “Who are some of the players on your team, underrated players you feel are going to have a breakout season for y’all this year?… Who do you feel is the X-factor for y’all to take that next step? I’m sure all of you guys need to step up, but who do you think is that guy that’s going to help push y’all over the top that not too many people know about?”
Judge: “I got three guys in mind… I’ll start with our second baseman, Jazz Chisholm. He had a great year last year. 30-30, did all that, but this kid’s talent, man. He can be one of the greats in the game. You know what I’m saying? So I think this year, especially, he’s about to be a free agent. I think this will be a big year for him to take that next step, take more of a leadership role, just take that role where, hey man, you want to be a face of a franchise, you want to be this and that, man. This is what you got to do. And I can just kind of see him, since the short time I’ve seen him since we got him, I see him taking those steps each year.”
Looking At Jazz
Chisholm Jr. (who is a two-time MLB All-Star) spent the first part of his career with the Miami Marlins.
He has been with New York for part of three seasons (and helped them reach the 2024 World Series).
There is no question that the 28-year-old will be among the most intriguing free agents on the market this winter.

item.content:encoded:
According to a recent report by New York reporter Jon Heyman, the Yankees were willing to part ways with shortstop George Lombard Jr. in a potential trade that would have involved Hunter Goodman.
Flashback to the 2026 MLB trade deadline: it was thought that the Yankees’ biggest target was a right-handed hitting catcher.
However, New York whiffed completely on upgrading at the catcher position, and that may or may not have led to an early exit in the MLB playoffs.
Now, fast-forward to the 2026 offseason, the Yankees are already being urged to try to trade for Hunter Goodman in a recovery-type move.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision
George Lombard Jr. Could Have Been Traded
Wow… wouldn’t it be something if the Yankees actually moved on from George Lombard Jr.?
It’s also an interesting report from the standpoint of thinking if there will be speculation surrounding Lombard Jr.’s roster status going forward.
George Lombard Jr. was a standout contributor for the Yankees down the stretch, and he’s entirely too young to give up on, but it’s clear the Yankees were trying to pull all the strings to acquire Hunter Goodman.
There’s also a side to this that the report from Heyman doesn’t have much substance behind it, because it doesn’t make sense for the Yankees front office to reveal any of the details in a potential blockbuster trade that didn’t happen months ago.
In 2026, Lombard Jr.’s first taste of MLB action, Lombard Jr. batted .237 with seven home runs, 22 RBI, and an OPS+ of 92 over 152 at-bats.
He’s just 21 years old.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Predicted to Poach Yankees All-Star for $80 Million
Buy or Sell This Yankees Trade Report Involving George Lombard Jr.?
New York Yankees fans, do you buy or sell this trade report regarding George Lombard Jr.?
Lombard Jr. did a lot of things the right way in his first MLB action, which doesn’t often happen, especially with players who are under the age of 2022.
George Lombard Jr. is expected to be a key piece of the New York Yankees’ future, and there are always growing pains along the way in any young star’s development.
Speaking quickly to the Hunter Goodman side of this report, which should also carry some weight, Goodman’s power at the catcher position right now is unmatched.
He’s smashed 72 home runs over the last two seasons and has a strong case to be the best power-hitting catcher in MLB right now.
Perhaps the Yankees can still try to acquire Goodman via trade, but it wouldn’t likely feature Lombard Jr.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees‘ season concluded exactly one week ago when the Tampa Bay Rays officially swept them in the NLDS.
The loss extended the Yankees’ streak without a World Series title to 17 seasons and marked the end of veteran right-handed pitcher Gerrit Cole’s 13th season in the league.
This was a big year for Cole after he missed a large portion of the beginning of the year and all of last season following Tommy John surgery in 2024.
Although it took some time, Cole put together a stellar 2026 campaign, posting a 10-9 record with a 3.61 ERA, 99 strikeouts and a 1.102 WHIP across 22 starts and 127 innings.
Cole Receives Major Personal News
On Wednesday, with the Yankees beginning their offseason, Cole received recognition for a prestigious personal honor announced by the MLBPA.
The MLBPA named Cole one of the finalists for the American League Comeback Player of the Year Award. The other two candidates were Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez and Los Angeles Angels outfielder Mike Trout.
The National League finalists included three pitchers: Sandy Alcantara of the Miami Marlins, Martin Perez of the Atlanta Braves and Zack Wheeler of the Philadelphia Phillies.

Cole’s MLB Career
This would be Cole’s first Comeback Player of the Year Award in his decade-plus career, which has spanned three teams.
Cole has spent the last six seasons with the Yankees. He began his career with the Pittsburgh Pirates, where he spent five years, before joining the Houston Astros for two seasons.
Throughout his career, Cole has earned six All-Star selections, won a Cy Young Award and claimed the ERA title twice.

item.title: [Bolavip US] Report: Ryan McMahon among expected offseason departures for NY Yankees
item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: Another MLB season has ended in disappointment for the New York Yankees. Despite entering the postseason with championship aspirations, the Yankees fell well short of expectations, suffering an early exit against the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. Now heading into the offseason, the front office is preparing for what could be a summer of major roster turnover. A report from The New York Post‘s Joel Sherman indicates that third baseman Ryan McMahon could be among those on the move. “The Yankees will
item.content:encoded:
Another MLB season has ended in disappointment for the New York Yankees. Despite entering the postseason with championship aspirations, the Yankees fell well short of expectations, suffering an early exit against the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. Now heading into the offseason, the front office is preparing for what could be a summer of major roster turnover.
A report from The New York Post‘s Joel Sherman indicates that third baseman Ryan McMahon could be among those on the move. “The Yankees will try hard to find a way to redirect McMahon’s money elsewhere as they look to improve the roster for 2027,” Sherman reported.
Sherman noted that moving McMahon is primarily a financial decision rather than a reflection of his play, as the veteran remains a valuable asset at third base. Still, after another underwhelming campaign, the Bronx Bombers must weigh every available option to clear payroll flexibility and reshape their roster.
Meanwhile, additional reports suggest the Yankees could turn their attention toward outfield help, potentially targeting Seattle Mariners star Randy Arozarena. Offloading McMahon’s contract would give New York the financial room needed to pursue Arozarena and other high-profile targets as they aim to bounce back in 2027.
Ryan McMahon #19 of the New York Yankees fields a bunt.
Losing McMahon could leave the Yankees with a major infield void
Ever since acquiring McMahon from the Colorado Rockies, the Yankees relied on him to anchor third base. Moving on from the veteran leaves a massive defensive hole at the hot corner, with no clear internal prospects ready to take over.
McMahon’s offense cratered after leaving Denver for the Bronx, as he slumped to a .216 batting average with negligible WAR production across the 2026 season. Trading or releasing him would represent a clear cut-your-losses move, allowing New York to wipe his remaining $16 million salary for 2027 off the books.
If the Yankees part ways with McMahon alongside free-agent decisions surrounding Jazz Chisholm Jr., general manager Brian Cashman faces an immediate offseason burden: securing external trade targets or free agents to fill multiple spots in the starting lineup.
Key takeaways
- Ryan McMahon may be moved by the Yankees to clear payroll for 2027.
- Clearing McMahon’s salary would help New York pursue Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena.
- Offloading McMahon leaves a $16 million salary gap and an unfilled third-base position.

It was a disappointing result for a team built to make it back to the World Series. Still, there were plenty of bright spots from the regular season, and one of them was certainly left fielder Cody Bellinger. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees season came to a crashing end last week when they were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. It was a disappointing result for a team built to make it back to the World Series.
Still, there were plenty of bright spots from the regular season, and one of them was certainly left fielder Cody Bellinger. The 31-year-old signed a five-year, $162.5 million deal with the Yankees last winter to extend his stay in the Bronx, and it worked out in New York’s favor.
He earned his third career All-Star selection this year and posted a .264 batting average, .338 on-base percentage and .768 OPS across 132 games.
That is not the only value Bellinger provided though. While he no longer suits up in center field, he has become one of the best defensive left fielders in baseball.
According to Baseball Savant, he posted a Fielding Run Value of 8 and an Outs Above Average of 6. His arm was also one of the best in the outfield, frequently deterring runners from taking an extra base.
As a result, he was nominated for an American League Gold Glove Award in left field on Wednesday. “Congratulations to our @RawlingsSports Gold Glove finalists: Austin Wells, Cody Bellinger & José Caballero ,” the Yankees wrote on X.
Congratulations to our @RawlingsSports Gold Glove finalists: Austin Wells, Cody Bellinger & José Caballero pic.twitter.com/by6aX06xFq
— New York Yankees (@Yankees) October 14, 2026
Fans were quick to congratulate Bellinger and the other nominees in the comments.
“Well deserved Belli ⚾️,” wrote a fan.
“Bellinger is very deserving,” added another.
One more said, “Really hoping Bellinger gets it, he deserves it after the amount of carrying he had to do.”
“Belli!!” wrote another.
“Bellinger should be the favorite,” said one fan.
Bellinger will have to beat out Wyatt Langford of the Texas Rangers and Chandler Simpson of the Rays. If he wins, it would mark the second Gold Glove of his career. Rawlings will announce the winners on Sunday, November 1st.

item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays have several decisions to make this offseason regarding their roster. After letting Bo Bichette walk in free agency a season ago, the Blue Jays endured some inconsistent play up the middle of their infield, so one would imagine that's a big point of emphasis for the front office. Well, in a recent predictions piece, the Blue Jays are linked to poaching away New York Yankees' All-Star Jazz Chisholm Jr. in free agency. More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Trade Pitch Dumps Ronal
item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays have several decisions to make this offseason regarding their roster.
After letting Bo Bichette walk in free agency a season ago, the Blue Jays endured some inconsistent play up the middle of their infield, so one would imagine that's a big point of emphasis for the front office.
Well, in a recent predictions piece, the Blue Jays are linked to poaching away New York Yankees' All-Star Jazz Chisholm Jr. in free agency.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Trade Pitch Dumps Ronald Acuña Jr. to Mariners for 2 Players
Blue Jays Predicted to Sign Jazz Chisholm Jr.
In a recent predictions piece by FanSided.com's John Perrotto, Jazz Chisholm Jr. is predicted to sign with the Blue Jays on a four-year, $80 million deal:
"Yankees fans are tired of Chisholm's inconsistency, booing him when the Rays eliminated New York in an ALDS, and he's expected to move on in free agency despite hitting 19 homers and stealing 41 bases in 137 games. Chisholm has power, speed and the versatility to play second base, third base and center field."
Perrotto makes a good point: the Yankees may be fed up with Chisholm Jr., but Jazz has noted he would like to stay in New York.
After an All-Star campaign in 2025, where Jazz recorded a 30/30 season, he was unable to back that up in 2026 with just 19 home runs and a below-average OPS+ (97).
However, he is still a very solid player, and while he's not a great defender in the "defensive runs saved" category, Chisholm Jr. makes up for it in the above-average outs and fielding run value categories.
If the Blue Jays are going to be big spenders again this offseason, which feels like the case, grabbing Jazz on a $20 million AAV deal seems pretty fair for both sides.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Trade Prediction Lands World Series MVP for Heliot Ramos, 2 Prospects
Is $80 Million Over Four Years Good Market Value for Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Let's be clear: while it's easy to say that Jazz didn't have a 'great' year at the plate, which could be true, it's not like the free-agent class for second basemen is absolutely loaded, and aside from Brandon Lowe, Chisholm Jr. is undoubtedly a top option in the class.
According to Spotrac.com, Chisholm's market value is two years, $34 million, which is an AAV of $17 million.
Add in inflation that teams like the Blue Jays are willing to pay for All-Star players, and you get a four-year, $80 million projection.
Perhaps the Jays overpay for Chisholm Jr., or they don't offer him a 4+ year deal, and instead land somewhere closer to what Spotrac.com projects.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Yankees insider's strong Ryan McMahon hint comes with a Teruaki Sato downer
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: To say that the Ryan McMahon era hasn't gone the way the New York Yankees planned is an understatement. Since arriving in the Bronx at the 2025 trade deadline, he's been among the absolute worst hitters in baseball. If that wasn't bad enough, his trademark defense fell off substantially in 2026, and one doesn't have to look further than Game 2 of the ALDS for proof. Finding a way to ditch McMahon and other deadweight on the roster, even if it means eating some cash, has been a core tenet of our
item.content:encoded:
To say that the Ryan McMahon era hasn't gone the way the New York Yankees planned is an understatement. Since arriving in the Bronx at the 2025 trade deadline, he's been among the absolute worst hitters in baseball. If that wasn't bad enough, his trademark defense fell off substantially in 2026, and one doesn't have to look further than Game 2 of the ALDS for proof.
Finding a way to ditch McMahon and other deadweight on the roster, even if it means eating some cash, has been a core tenet of our plan to restore the Yankees' former glory. Whether or not they'd actually be so bold, though, remained to be seen.
Last week, Yankees insider Joel Sherman laid out some possibilities as to how New York could flip McMahon for a more useful part in a column for the New York Post. All of the solutions he laid out were essentially bad-contract-for-bad-contract swaps, like sending McMahon to the Giants in exchange for Harrison Bader or to the Twins in exchange for Victor Caratini.
Then, on the Pinstripe Post podcast a week later, Sherman doubled down, saying, "I think that the Yankees will try very hard to redirect Ryan McMahon's money, which is $16 million in the last season, someplace else. Do they eat it? Like, do they get him down to a $5 million player, and that allows them to get a relief pitcher or something?"
Sherman then reiterated that they could pursue bad contract swaps, acquiring players who might fit a need better on the roster, even if they are overpaid.
Moving on from McMahon obviously opens up a hole at third base, and unfortunately, the free-agent market is primarily made up of past-their-prime veterans at the hot corner, as well as utility men. The one exception is Japanese star Teruaki Sato, who is expected to be posted by the NPB's Hanshin Tigers. He's left Yankees fans salivating about his potential for a while.
Unfortunately, Sherman doesn't see New York making the big splash for Sato, citing defensive concerns. He did, however, highlight the importance of the club re-establishing prominence in the Japanese market and pointed to some hires made over the past year in the international scouting department as being crucial first steps towards that goal.
Prioritizing defense over offense in a Ryan McMahon replacement could be a Yankees' mistake
There are no bones about it: the Yankees need to tighten up their defense, as it has repeatedly let them down in big spots like the 2024 World Series and the 2026 ALDS. However, focusing too much on defense and ignoring offensive concerns is what gives you Oswald Peraza, and then ultimately McMahon, as your starting third baseman.
The 27-year-old Sato has been compared to Chicago White Sox darling Munetaka Murakami, and to an extent, the comparison is apt. Murakami had played third base in the past, but was ultimately thought of as a better firt at first base. Sato, who played 125 games at third base while making 19 errors this year at the position, also has experience playing right field. While he's never played first, there are some who believe that's where he'll ultimately end up.
That's what gives Sherman pause, not just because first base is a less valuable position than the hot corner, but because of the Yankees' roster construction. Ben Rice and Luis Garcia Jr. are already two left-handed hitters splitting time between first and DH, so adding another lefty bat in Sato could result in a third player being parked in that rotation as well.
Throw in Aaron Judge likely getting a healthy dose of DH days, and it starts to become very difficult to see how the pieces all fit in the same lineup on a daily basis.
To an extent, it doesn't matter. Sato is 27 years old, and should be given a year to prove beyond a shadow of a doubt that he can or cannot handle the hot corner. If he can't, there's always the possibility of moving him to a corner outfield spot and letting Cody Bellinger take over center field full time.
More importantly, the Yankees have something of a reset on their hands in Japan with a new regime taking over the scouting department. By not making a big splash now, they'll be sending the message that it'll be more of the same, and it will put them even further behind the eight ball when it comes to revitalizing a market that they once dominated.
The defensive concerns shouldn't be overlooked, but at the same time, the cost of not pursuing Sato is greater. This is about present-day priorities as much as it is about the future. For the Yankees, it seems as if they're willing to forgo future opportunities in service of reacting to an immediate problem, if Sherman's read on the situation is correct. That could be a mistake.

item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees fans were disappointed with the outcome of their favorite team’s season, to say the least.
The Yankees finished the regular season with 93 wins and swept the Boston Red Sox 2-0 in the American League Wild Card Series.
Then it all went downhill. The Tampa Bay Rays absolutely embarrassed the Yankees in the American League Division Series, sweeping their rival 3-0 en route to advancing to the American League Championship Series. The Rays are now playing the Guardians in the ALCS.
While the outcome of the season has left a bad taste in most Yankees fans’ mouths, one positive they can take away is the outstanding season of right-hander Cam Schlittler, who just received exciting personal news.
New York Yankees’ Cam Schlittler Gets Exciting Personal News Amid Playoffs
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – SEPTEMBER 29: Cam Schlittler #31 of the New York Yankees throws a pitch against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning in game one of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 29, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images)
The Major League Baseball Players Association announces its finalists for the 2026 Players Choice Awards.
Schlittler is one of the three finalists for the AL Outstanding Pitcher Award.
PHOENIX, ARIZONA – SEPTEMBER 19: Starting pitcher Cam Schlittler #31 of the New York Yankees throws a warm-up pitch during the first inning of the MLB game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on September 19, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images)
Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays and Sonny Gray of the Boston Red Sox are the other finalists for the award.
MLBPA wrote on X:
🚨 Congratulations to the 2026 Players Choice Awards Finalists!🚨
Since 1992, the Players Choice Awards have celebrated excellence across Major League Baseball, recognizing performance, leadership, perseverance, and impact on and off the field. The awards are especially meaningful to players, because they’re determined through a vote of their peers. The winners will be revealed the week of Oct 26. Congratulations to this year’s Finalists!
Looking at New York Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JULY 24: Cam Schlittler #31 of the New York Yankees pitches during a game against the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on July 24, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Schlittler is the clear favorite to win the Outstanding Pitcher Award.
He led the AL in bWAR (7.0), ERA (1.95) and ERA+ (215) this year. He collected 239 strikeouts over 193 2/3 innings.
TORONTO, CANADA – JUNE 13: Cam Schlittler #31 of the New York Yankees pitches against the Toronto Blue Jays during the third inning in their MLB game at the Rogers Centre on June 13, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Mark Blinch/Getty Images)
During the playoffs, Schlittler allowed four runs (two earned) in 10 2/3 innings across two starts while striking out 12.
Schlittler made his MLB debut last season. In his rookie year, Schlittler recorded a 2.96 ERA with 84 strikeouts over 73 innings.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] NY Yankees shouldn't give up on their catcher just yet
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Austin Wells’ .186 average is going to follow him through the winter. Fair enough. He had a bad season at the plate, and nobody needs to pretend otherwise. I wouldn’t use that number to decide the Yankees’ entire catching plan, though. item.content:encoded:
Austin Wells’ .186 average is going to follow him through the winter. Fair enough. He had a bad season at the plate, and nobody needs to pretend otherwise.
I wouldn’t use that number to decide the Yankees’ entire catching plan, though. His second half was substantially better, and the most useful addition might be somebody who covers the matchup he still hasn’t solved rather than somebody who replaces him outright.
The renewed offseason debate is legitimate. Joel Sherman put catcher first in his Monday position-by-position review for the New York Post. New York can’t enter 2027 assuming Wells’ worst stretch won’t happen again. It also shouldn’t evaluate him as if that stretch lasted all year.
Two very different versions of the Yankees catcher
Wells hit .155/.247/.258 before the All-Star break, with six homers in 220 plate appearances. After it, he hit .229/.351/.436 with eight homers in 168 plate appearances. His OPS rose from .505 to .787.
The average remained modest. The improvement in reaching base and hitting for power was much more useful: 24 walks in each half despite 52 fewer plate appearances after the break. His strikeout rate fell from 27.7% to 25%, calculated from those same regular-season totals.
It would be premature to declare him fixed. Ignoring the improvement would be unfair too. A catcher producing a .351 on-base percentage contributes to an offense even when he isn’t piling up singles.
The backup has to solve a specific matchup
Wells’ full-season numbers against left-handers were rough: .122/.192/.244 in 99 plate appearances. Against righties, he had a .326 on-base percentage and .691 OPS in 289 plate appearances. The second-half improvement and the left-handed-pitching issue can both be true.
Pay for a useful partner
I’d look for a right-handed catcher who can take meaningful starts against lefties, rather than sign a backup the staff barely wants to use. That would give Wells fewer bad matchups and give the Yankees a real option when he needs a day off. It wouldn’t require finding an expensive everyday catcher merely to make a statement after a disappointing year.
A full replacement becomes more attractive if a clearly better two-way catcher is available at a sensible price. Wells’ second half doesn’t rule that out. Nor do his hitting splits measure everything a catcher does defensively; receiving, throwing and working with the staff belong in that decision too.
The Yankees shouldn’t promise him the job regardless of performance. They should give the improved version a chance with useful support. If he carries that on-base production into next year and the new partner handles the lefty starts, New York can improve the position without throwing away the progress Wells actually made.

item.content:encoded:
How active will the New York Yankees be in trade this offseason??
After a disappointing 2026 campaign, it’s fair to assume the Yanks’ front office will be doing everything to better set up the roster for the 2027 season, which means meaningful trades could be on the horizon.
One recent trade rumor suggests the Yankees could be a player in a deal for Houston Astros shortstop Jeremy Peña.
More MLB on Heavy: Yankees Urged to Trade for Rangers’ All-Star Infielder
Would the Yankees Trade for Jeremy Peña?
Recently, FanSided.com’s John Perotto put out a trade rumors/free agency predictions piece for some of MLB’s biggest stars, and the MLB writer predicts the Yankees will trade for Jeremy Peña:
“Prediction: Traded to Yankees for outfielder Heliot Ramos, right-hander Brendan Beck and shortstop Dax Kilby (Yankees’ No. 2 prospect, MLB’s No. 36)”
He also wrote (about why Peña could be a hot commodity this offseason);
“Peña etched his name in Astros history in 2022, when he was the MVP of both the ALCS and World Series as a rookie. However, Peña’ time in Houston could be well over, as he is eligible for free agency at the end of next season and will likely earn at least $13 million through arbitration. Plenty of teams will be interested in a 29-year-old shortstop who hit .277/.325/.477 with 22 home runs and 12 stolen bases in 112 games,”
It creates an interesting question that the Yankees would have to solve with George Lombard Jr. and Jeremy Peña on the same side of the diamond.
Peña has a strong arm, so if the Yankees didn’t want to mess with the development of George Lombard Jr., they could move Peña to third, and leave Lombard Jr. at short, but this is a trade scenario where the Yankees could kill a couple of birds with one stone by offloading Heliot Ramos (who was disappointing since being traded to New York), and finding a much-needed 3B with strong production with the bat.
One rebuttal to the trade idea that’s worth mentioning is that this is quite a large trade haul for the Yankees to give up for a potential rental addition, so in order to justify the trade, New York would have to ink Peña to a contract extension at some point after *potentially* trading for him.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Predicted to Sign 2X MLB All-Star to Replace Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Taking a Closer Look at Jeremy Peña….
Jeremy Peña has quietly been one of the game’s most productive infielders over the past several seasons.
He’s a tenured 5-year MLB veteran with 680 games played.
Across those 680 games, and 2640 total at-bats, Pena is batting .272 with 86 home runs, 303 RBI, and 76 stolen bases.
His lifetime OPS+ is 109, but he’s coming off a strong 2026 campaign, where his OPS+ was 126.
In the past two seasons, Peña has logged an OPS+ north of 125.
Yankees fans, would you consider making this trade?? Why or why not??
And if not, who would you like to see Brian Cashman and company try to acquire this offseason?

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Insider Reveals Austin Wells Decision Ahead of 2027
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The New York Yankees enter the offseason with questions to answer across the roster. The pitching staff needs reinforcement. The lineup needs a right-handed bat. Free agency decisions loom at multiple positions. One position appears to have a clearer direction. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees enter the offseason with questions to answer across the roster. The pitching staff needs reinforcement. The lineup needs a right-handed bat. Free agency decisions loom at multiple positions.
One position appears to have a clearer direction. Behind the plate, the Yankees have signaled where they stand despite a season that did not always make the decision easy.
What Sherman Reported
According to MLB insider Joel Sherman of the New York Post, Austin Wells is expected to remain New York's starting catcher heading into 2027.
Sherman's report indicates that while the Yankees acknowledge Wells' offensive inconsistencies, the organization views him as their catcher moving forward. Wells caught 122 games in 2026 and earned the trust of the pitching staff with his work behind the plate.
The decision is tied to more than just production. Wells is projected to earn approximately $2.6 million through arbitration for 2027. Keeping him as the starter allows the Yankees to allocate their spending toward other areas of need rather than investing heavily at a position they believe is accounted for.
The Numbers Behind the Yankees Decision
Wells struggled badly in the first half of the season, posting a .155 batting average with a .258 slugging percentage. The swing looked off. The results were not close to what the Yankees expected from a former first-round pick.
Then something shifted after the All-Star break. Wells hit .229 with an OPS north of .780 and a 120 OPS+ across the second half. He drew more walks, drove the ball with authority, and looked like a different hitter than the one who had frustrated the fanbase for months.
He carried that into October, going 5-for-17 with four walks across two postseason rounds. The bat showed signs of life when it mattered most.
The Search for a Platoon Partner
The Yankees are expected to pursue a right-handed platoon partner to complement the left-handed-hitting Wells. Sherman identified several potential options, including Freddy Fermin, Austin Hedges, Victor Caratini, Luis Campusano, and Gary Sanchez.
The catcher search is not new territory for the front office. New York actively pursued Ryan Jeffers before the trade deadline, but the Twins got hot in late July and opted to hold onto him. Hunter Goodman was another name the Yankees discussed with Colorado, though the Rockies' asking price was steep.
Finding the right complement matters. Wells' splits against left-handed pitching have been a weakness, and adding a right-handed bat behind him would address that gap without requiring the Yankees to move on from their starter entirely.
Final Word for the Yankees
Wells is expected to be behind the plate on Opening Day. The second half and the postseason gave the Yankees enough reason to believe the bat is trending in the right direction.
If Sherman's reporting holds, the starting job is Wells' to lose heading into 2027. A full season of the version that showed up after July would go a long way toward silencing the debate.

item.content:encoded:
On October 7, the New York Yankees had their season come to an end when they lost to the Tampa Bay Rays by a score of 4-3 in the Bronx.
The Yankees got swept by the Rays (and have lost in the ALDS for the second straight year).
Yankee Star Issues Heartfelt Message
After their season came to an end, Heliot Ramos made a post to Instagram (on October 13).
He wrote: “The season ends. The hunger stays. ⚾️🔥 Thank you to my teammates, my family, and everyone who showed up for me along the way. Taking the memories, the lessons, and the drive to come back stronger. Proud to carry Puerto Rico with me every time I step on the field. 🇵🇷 More to come.”
Ramos did not play in the final game of the season.
He batted .198 with four home runs and 12 RBIs in 38 games for the Yankees.
The 27-year-old also appeared in one MLB playoff game.
Looking At Ramos
Heliot Ramos #34 of the New York Yankees rounds the bases after hitting a triple against the Baltimore Orioles during their game at Yankee Stadium on September 25, 2026 in New York City.
Ramos spent the first 4.5 seasons of his career with the San Francisco Giants.
He made the 2024 MLB All-Star Game when he batted .269 with 22 home runs and 72 RBIs in 121 games.
The Giants traded him to the Yankees during the middle of the 2026 season.
The Yankees wrote (via X) on August 3: “The New York Yankees today announced that they have acquired outfielder Heliot Ramos from the San Francisco Giants in exchange for minor league infielder Kaeden Kent and left-handed pitcher Henry Lalane.”
Looking At The Yankees
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees looks on during batting practice before game one of the American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on October 03, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
The Yankees had another strong regular season where they were the second-place team in the American League East with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
That said, the franchise has been unable to win a World Series title since the 2009 season when Derek Jeter, CC Sabathia and Alex Rodriguez were still on the roster.

item.content:encoded:
Joe Girardi isn’t blaming Aaron Boone for the Yankees’ shortcomings, but believes a deeper-rooted culture issue might have contributed to the team being swept in the ALDS.
The former Yankees skipper tore into the team’s fundamentals, pointing to a pair of costly postseason blunders that underscored his concerns during an appearance on “The Show with Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman.”




Access the Yankees beat like never before

Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
“There are things that happen and you wonder, ‘Is someone saying anything?’” Girardi said on The Post podcast.
Girardi cited Austin Wells’ baserunning blunder in Game 1 and Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s disastrous throw in an error-filled Game 2 as examples of the team’s fundamental failures — and the concerning response to those mistakes.
Chisholm, in particular, said, “I’d probably still try to throw it,” if given a do-over, despite the result of the play.
“You said you would’ve done the same thing over again? No! You can’t do the same thing again — it didn’t work!” Girardi added. “Some of the base running cues, the sliding over the bases, someone’s gotta say, ‘Enough is enough!’”
Girardi, who managed the Yankees from 2009-17, noted that the sloppy play needs to be addressed during the regular season, especially with underperforming players.
He referenced infielder Anthony Volpe, who had been New York’s incumbent shortstop the past three seasons before being demoted to Triple-A midseason.
“I think it happened with Anthony Volpe,” Girardi added. “I think he was better when he came back up because he sent down and said, ‘Hey, I can’t keep doing what I’m doing, it’s not working.'”
Girardi, 62, knows the trappings and challenges of managing the Bombers all too well. He led the club to a World Series title in 2009 but, despite reaching the ALCS in 2017, he was let go as skipper and replaced by Boone.
In what’s expected to be a transformative offseason for the Yankees, Girardi went to bat for Boone, whose future has come under fire in the wake of another abrupt postseason exit.
Girardi said that 2026 is arguably Boone’s best year, citing the team finishing with the American League’s second-best record despite a rash of injuries and down seasons from key players.
“Can you say that that’s his fault? I don’t think so,” Girardi said. “To me, that’s not his fault. I just don’t think the guys had the years that they projected them to have, or some of the guys just aren’t as good as they thought they would be.”

item.content:encoded:
Perhaps the biggest question the New York Yankees will have to answer this offseason is whether they should retain Jazz Chisholm Jr., or let him walk in MLB free agency.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. has noted he would like to return to the Yankees on a long-term deal, but who wouldn't want to ink a deal with the big-spending Yankees during their free agency, which often leads to big-day pay.
However, the Yankees' front office may not be open to a Jazz Chisholm Jr. reunion, which has led to speculation of other free agents New York could sign to replace Mr. Chisholm Jr.
One player that stands out is second baseman Brandon Lowe, who recently played for the Pittsburgh Pirates.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Urged to Part Ways with 7X MLB All-Star in Offseason Move
Yankees Could Make Major Brandon Lowe Signing to Fix Jazz Chisholm Jr. Problem
In a recent rumors piece by Bleacher Report.com's Zach Buckley, the New York Yankees are predicted to sign Brandon Lowe in free agency:
"Maybe the Pirates' 82 wins, their most since 2018, will embolden them to spend, though Lowe's contract could feature both a big annual salary and a good amount of years. That combination might be more than Pittsburgh's front office can stomach, which would be music to the ears of a certain major-market big-spender with question marks at Lowe's second base position."
"Prediction: Lowe signs with the New York Yankees."
Lowe batted .260 in 2026 with 35 home runs, 96 RBI, and an OPS+ of 121. He was not named an MLB All-Star, but he certainly posted All-Star caliber numbers.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. may demand more money in free agency than Lowe, and he didn't put up nearly as strong offensive numbers.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are overflowing with impending free agents as they enter their 2026 offseason.
Rumors stay afloat, but some come with more substance than others.
An MLB insider uncovered his latest prediction for one of the Yankees’ top free agents.
Yankees Insider Predicts David Bednar’s Future in New York
Chris Kirschner of The Athletic didn’t hold back his thoughts regarding 32-year-old reliever David Bednar.
If his prediction becomes reality, Bednar will return to New York for his 2027 campaign.
“Some players fold when they join the Yankees after coming from clubs with no winning expectations, but not Bednar, who turned 32 on Saturday,” he wrote. “He’s as dependable as a closer can get in today’s game, converting 35 of 39 save chances this season. That’s why the Yankees should extend him the qualifying offer, with the ultimate goal of locking in a multi-year extension.
By the end of Bednar’s 2026 regular season, he had registered a 2.47 ERA and 76 strikeouts across 69.1 innings of work through 64 games. He walked 20 batters.
This was only his first season sporting the Yankees’ iconic pinstripes.
The San Diego Padres selected him 1,044th overall in the 35th round of the 2016 MLB draft. He made his big league debut in September 2019.
Before landing in the Northeast, Bednar played a two-year stint with the Padres, followed by a five-year stint with the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Once July 2025 rolled around, the Pirates traded him to New York in exchange for minor leaguers Edgleen Perez and Brian Sanchez, along with Rafael Flores.
Staying with the Yankees would likely come with less immediate risk. He’s reliable, and he’s experienced — two valuable ingredients for any bullpen.
Snapshot of the Yankees Ahead of Hot Stove Season
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – OCTOBER 07: Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees signals toward the bullpen during the eighth inning in game three of the American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on October 07, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
New York’s 2026 campaign came, it went, and now we’re quickly approaching the chaotic hot stove season.
This is the point in the year when we will start to see ballclubs make colossal waves with free agent signings and shocking trades. Rosters inevitably rattle.
The Yankees need consistency, which is something they are struggling with this year.
Of course, unexpected injuries were a major contributor to their inconsistency, but New York needs to shake up its roster.
When they entered this season, there were very few changes to their roster.
Looking ahead to 2027, this might not be the case.
Sure, they might be able to retain Bednar. However, stars Jazz Chisholm Jr., Paul Goldschmidt and Trent Grisham are also impending free agents.
The likelihood of each one staying in New York is slim.

item.content:encoded:
El pelotero panameño José Caballero se unió a las iniciativas de apoyo a las familias afectadas por el terremoto que sacudió Panamá y dejó consecuencias en distintas zonas del interior del país.
El jugador de los Yankees de Nueva York anunció que, junto a su esposa, Carvalho Family Foundation y el Consulado de Panamá en Nueva York, organizará una recolecta para enviar ayuda a quienes más lo necesitan.
Caballero compartió un video en sus redes sociales en el que explicó que la iniciativa busca llegar a familias que atraviesan una situación difícil, algunas de ellas incomunicadas y con dificultades para solicitar asistencia.
“Quiero hablarles en nombre de todas las familias panameñas que están pasando por un momento muy difícil, muchas de estas incomunicadas y sin poder alzar la voz y pedir ayuda, por eso mi esposa y junto a Carvalho Family Foundation y el Consulado de Panamá acá en Nueva York nos unimos para hacer una recolecta y hacerle llegar a quienes los necesitan”, expresó el jugador.
El infielder también hizo un llamado a los panameños que viven en Nueva York, al resto de la comunidad panameña en Estados Unidos y a cualquier persona que pueda contribuir con la iniciativa.
“Hago un llamado a todas las personas, todos los panameños que estamos acá en Nueva York, en Estados Unidos entero y a cualquier persona que pueda darnos la mano y apoyar a nuestras familias panameñas que la están pasando súper difícil, que cada granito cuenta, cada granito se le va a hacer llegar a las personas necesitadas y de verdad que se lo agradeceríamos mucho”, manifestó.
La iniciativa busca canalizar la solidaridad de la comunidad panameña en el extranjero para brindar apoyo a las personas que enfrentan las consecuencias del sismo. Caballero destacó la importancia de cada aporte para ayudar a las familias que atraviesan este momento complicado.
El pelotero viene de una temporada en las Grandes Ligas con los Yankees de Nueva York en la que bateó para promedio de .231, conectó 14 cuadrangulares e impulsó 51 carreras en 136 partidos.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] NY Yankees could try to unload a $16M disappointment
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Joel Sherman thinks the Yankees will try to move Ryan McMahon’s contract this offseason. After another rough year at the plate, I would be looking for an exit too. “I think the Yankees will try very hard to see if they can redirect Ryan McMahon’s money someplace else,” Sherman said. item.content:encoded:
Joel Sherman thinks the Yankees will try to move Ryan McMahon’s contract this offseason. After another rough year at the plate, I would be looking for an exit too.
“I think the Yankees will try very hard to see if they can redirect Ryan McMahon’s money someplace else,” Sherman said.
That’s Sherman’s expectation, not confirmation that the Yankees have opened trade talks or found a buyer. The distinction matters, because wanting to move a contract and getting a useful deal are two different things.
Why the Yankees should at least explore it
McMahon finished the 2026 regular season hitting .213/.279/.357 with 11 home runs and 41 RBIs in 124 games. His .636 OPS gives the Yankees plenty of reason to reconsider their plans at third base.
The strikeouts remained a problem. He struck out 106 times in 360 plate appearances, a 29.4% rate, and drew 28 walks. There were productive days, but not enough of them to offset how often he made an out. A .279 on-base percentage puts a lot of pressure on the power to carry the bat, and 11 homers didn’t do that.
McMahon is due $16 million in 2027, the final season of his six-year, $70 million contract. That salary is difficult to justify if the Yankees no longer see him as an everyday answer.
I’d rather they admit the fit hasn’t worked than hand him the job again because the money is already committed. The contract shouldn’t decide the lineup. It should make the front office look harder at whether that roster spot can be used more effectively.
A salary dump isn’t automatically a roster upgrade
The catch is that another club gets to read the same stat line. The Yankees can want payroll relief all they like, but a buyer would need a reason to take on the obligation. A team that sees a fix in McMahon’s approach might value him differently; that doesn’t establish an actual market or an interested club.
Paying down the deal is one possible way to make a trade work. If the Yankees covered $8 million and another team assumed the other $8 million, the cash savings would be $8 million, not $16 million. That’s an illustration, not a reported offer, and it doesn’t calculate any luxury-tax effect.
New York would also need to account for the cost of replacing him. Saving part of the salary only to spend it on another third baseman who doesn’t improve the offense wouldn’t accomplish much. Taking back a different expensive contract could help if the player fits better, but it wouldn’t necessarily reduce payroll.
I wouldn’t attach a worthwhile prospect just to get the entire salary off the books. If the available deals demand that, keeping McMahon and making him compete for playing time is a reasonable fallback. One season remains on the contract; there’s no reason to create a longer-term problem simply to finish a trade.
The Yankees would need to know who replaces McMahon before treating a trade as progress. Paying part of his salary can be a reasonable cost of getting a better player into the lineup, but losing a good prospect for payroll relief alone isn’t a deal I’d make.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Birthday of the Day: Charlie Silvera
item.dc:creator: Matt Ferenchick
item.description: As far as non-stressful jobs in sports go, backup catcher to an established star would be a pretty good one to have. For nine years in New York, Charlie Silvera got to fill that role, and not just behind any old star — he was the backup to Yankees icon Yogi Berra. For his career in the Bronx, Silvera made less than 500 plate appearances, yet he still got to play a role on one of the most successful eras in the history of the most successful franchise. Charles Anthony Ryan "Charlie" Silvera Born:
item.content:encoded:
As far as non-stressful jobs in sports go, backup catcher to an established star would be a pretty good one to have. For nine years in New York, Charlie Silvera got to fill that role, and not just behind any old star — he was the backup to Yankees icon Yogi Berra. For his career in the Bronx, Silvera made less than 500 plate appearances, yet he still got to play a role on one of the most successful eras in the history of the most successful franchise.
Charles Anthony Ryan "Charlie" Silvera
Born: October 13, 1924 (San Francisco, CA)
Died: September 7, 2019 (Millbrae, CA)
Yankees Tenure: 1948-56
Silvera was born in San Francisco in 1924, going on to become one of a number of Yankees of that era to hail from the city. In his youth, he played sandlot baseball with fellow future Yankees Bobby Brown and Jerry Coleman. In 1942, he caught the eye of the Yankees, who signed him to a deal.
Silvera debuted in the minors as a 17-year old in 1942, playing for the Class D Wellsville (NY) Yankees as an outfielder. However after 75 games there that season, he joined the military, serving in the Air Force in World War II. Silvera would miss the entirety of the next three seasons while serving, although he did play on a military team during that time.
Upon returning to baseball, the Yankees converted Silvera into a catcher. He spent the next three seasons in the minors before earning a call-up to the Yankees late in the 1948 season. He appeared in four games, recording three hits in both of his first two games, and going 8-for-14 in total.
After that cameo, Silvera earned the Yankees' backup job for the 1949 season. He would spend the next nine seasons filling that role. The most games he ever appeared in a season came in his full debut year in '49. Starter Yogi Berra missed some time through injury and Silvera hit decently enough in his 58 games that season, putting up a .315 batting average and a .403 OBP. However, he was never going to fully replace the budding star in Berra, and never would. The Yankees also advanced to the 1949 World Series. Silvera came off the bench in Game 2 of the series, as Berra again had to exit due to injury. He went 0-for-2, as the Yankees lost that game but won the series. Despite playing in an era where the Yankees were winning and playing in the Fall Classic a lot, that was the only postseason appearance Silvera would ever make.
Over the next seven seasons, Silvera played in just 18, 18, 20, 42, 20, 14, and seven games respectively. Despite that, he would win five more World Series rings during his time with the Yankees. Opposing players would often try to trash talk Silvera for his lack of playing time, but the catcher was never bothered. He later said "the opposition would call me 'Jesse James, the payroll bandit.' I'd tell them, 'Go ahead and give it to me, but Yogi Berra tips me more than you make.'"
Having only appeared in 21 games over his last two seasons in the Bronx, the Yankees traded Silvera to the Cubs ahead of the 1957 season. Silvera put up a completely respectable — for a backup catcher — 86 OPS+ with the Yankees, he was just never going to replace Berra.
Upon going to the Cubs, Silvera was given the No. 8 that Berra wore in New York. He appeared in 26 games for Chicago that season, but struggled and missed time with injury. The Cubs released him after that season. Silvera played a couple more years in the minors but never made it back to the bigs, leaving the playing ranks after 1960.
Silvera stayed in baseball in various roles after his playing career ended. He joined former teammate Billy Martin on the coaching staffs of the Twins, Tigers, and Rangers when Martin was beginning his managerial career. He served as the bullpen coach for those teams, although Martin didn't bring him back to the Bronx when Martin went back there.
After coaching, Silvera got into scouting with the Cubs and Marlins. He received a seventh World Series ring for his work for the 1997 Marlins. He often came back for Yankees Old-Timers' Day but he did return to the San Francisco area in his later years, where he resided until his passing in 2019. Prior to his death, he had been the last surviving member of the Yankees dynasty to win five championships in a row from 1949-53.
Had he played in the modern era, Silvera very likely could've gone to another team in free agency to get more playing time. However, the rules at the time were what they were, and the Yankees were plenty happy to keep him around as a backup. Ending up with more than a hand's worth of World Series rings would be a nice consolation prize.
See more of the "Yankees Birthday of the Day" series here.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Paul Blackburn's next Yankees deal can't be based on ERA alone
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: I would try to bring Paul Blackburn back. I wouldn’t give him a long contract on the assumption that the Yankees just found a reliever who will run a 1.59 ERA every year. Those positions aren’t contradictory. Blackburn was excellent over 85 innings in 2026, and replacing that much useful work is an actual offseason expense. His next deal still needs to reflect more than the most flattering number on his stat line. What the Yankees would actually be paying for Blackburn made 62 appearances, inclu
item.content:encoded:
I would try to bring Paul Blackburn back. I wouldn’t give him a long contract on the assumption that the Yankees just found a reliever who will run a 1.59 ERA every year.
Those positions aren’t contradictory. Blackburn was excellent over 85 innings in 2026, and replacing that much useful work is an actual offseason expense. His next deal still needs to reflect more than the most flattering number on his stat line.
What the Yankees would actually be paying for
Blackburn made 62 appearances, including two starts, and finished with a 1.08 WHIP. Opponents hit .195 against him. A pitcher who can give the club that much work without allowing many baserunners has obvious value, particularly when the bullpen needs more than three outs from somebody.
He also struck out 69 hitters and walked 33. His 7.31 strikeouts per nine innings were lower than his 7.85 rate in 2025, while his walks per nine rose from 2.77 to 3.49. The comparison uses his combined 2025 major-league season rather than his short Yankees stint alone.
That doesn’t erase his improvement. It does mean the ERA drop wasn’t accompanied by a jump in strikeouts or better walk control. I’d want the Yankees to price the full profile rather than treat the run prevention as a guarantee.
The runners already on base complicate it
Eleven of the 27 runners Blackburn inherited scored, or 40.7%. Those runs generally belong to the pitcher who put them on, so they don’t appear as earned runs on Blackburn’s record.
Twenty-seven runners is a small sample, and the number doesn’t tell us which bases were occupied, how many outs he inherited or what the defense did behind him. It would be unfair to declare him incapable of handling a jam from that figure alone. It would also be careless to ignore it when deciding whether to pay him like a top late-inning strikeout arm.
For me, the fit is a dependable pitcher who can start an inning, keep the game close and occasionally cover more than three outs. Bringing him back for that job leaves room to pursue a different type of reliever for situations where the Yankees need a strikeout with runners on.
Blackburn is headed toward free agency, so the team won’t get to set the price by itself. Another club may be willing to pay more for his innings and results. There’s no reported offer or bidding war behind my concern; it’s how I’d approach the decision before negotiations start.
A short multiyear deal would be reasonable if the cost still allows the Yankees to improve the rest of the bullpen. I’d be much less comfortable adding years just to beat another offer. Blackburn has earned a raise and a serious retention effort, but the Yankees need to pay for the job they want him to do, not buy the ERA and figure out the role afterward.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are entering the offseason with plenty of questions surrounding their roster.
The Yankees were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the NLDS and now have some decisions to make. It is clear that they need to improve their roster if they hope to have more success in 2027.
One of the Yankees’ biggest decisions this offseason is about star infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. The 28-year-old is a pending unrestricted free agent, and New York must decide if they want to bring him back. Given how shaky Chisholm’s 2026 season went, it would not be too surprising if both sides parted ways.
Yet, if the Yankees do not re-sign Chisholm, it would create a major hole in their infield. Due to this, the Yankees would need to find a replacement for him if he walked.
When looking at potential replacements for Chisholm, Atlanta Braves star Ozzie Albies stands out as a fascinating option. The 29-year-old would be a good player for New York to trade for if Chisholm does not return.
Braves’ Albies Is Creating Chatter in Rumor Mill & Yankees Should Target Him
Albies recently entered the rumor mill as a potential trade candidate. In a recent article for Bleacher Report, Joel Reuter named Albies one of baseball’s top offseason trade candidates to watch.
“Albies has spent his entire 10-year career with the Braves, tallying 25.7 WAR while earning four All-Star selections and winning two Silver Slugger awards,” Reuter wrote. “The surface-level power production was there once again, but he has posted a middling 88 OPS+ and .299 on-base percentage in 1,350 plate appearances the last two years, and the Braves could be ready to move on as part of a larger retooling.”
If the Braves make Albies available, the Yankees would be wise to target him. He has been a star throughout his career and could be a solid replacement for Chisholm. Due to this, he is among the players who the Yankees should have on their radar this offseason.
Albies Could Thrive With the Yankees
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 04: Ozzie Albies #1 of the Atlanta Braves looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Dodgers in game two of the National League Division Series at Dodger Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images)
Albies would have the potential to thrive with the Yankees. He has been a very good player on the Braves for years now, so he has shown that he can handle playing for a top contender. Thus, it would not be too surprising if he had success on a team like the Yankees if acquired.
Albies is still an effective player at this point in his career, too. In 162 games last season for the Braves, he posted 22 home runs, 73 RBI, and a .237 batting average. He has also hit at least 22 home runs in five seasons of his MLB career. This included in 2023 when he hit a career-high 33 homers. With this, he could give the Yankees’ roster more pop.
Nevertheless, it will be interesting to see if the Yankees pursue Albies this offseason. If the Yankees let Chisholm walk and he signs elsewhere, Albies would make sense as a strong replacement for him.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will have a chance to keep Jazz Chisholm Jr. this offseason.
He’s heading for free agency, but the Yankees aren’t shy about offering sizable contracts to players they want to keep.
The problem here is that the Yanks may decide they aren’t willing to pay Chisholm what he would want to stick around, which could result in him finding a new home in free agency.
This is actually Chisholm’s first foray into free agency. He was with the Miami Marlins to begin his career, and he came to the Yankees via trade.
Now, Chisholm has a chance to cash in. That payday might come from an unexpected place.
Jazz Chisholm Predicted Landing Spot
Bleacher Report’s Zachary D. Rymer wrote in a new article on Tuesday about where he thinks Chisholm might up, and it’s a fascinating move — the Los Angeles Angels.
Chisholm would be the Angels’ latest attempt to get Mike Trout to the playoffs for the first time in more than a decade.
“Chisholm could be in for a multi-year deal,” Rymer writes. “Yet after falling well short of his 50-50 goal and posting just 1.7 rWAR this year, the 28-year-old might be better off pursuing a one-year contract and reentering the market next winter. The Angels are just one of many teams that would have to be interested in such a deal. They are in need of help at the keystone, specifically, and upside on offense, generally. Chisholm can provide both, and some energy to boot. Depending on when the sale is finalized, signing Chisholm would also be a relatively low-risk way for Stan Kroenke to ingratiate himself with his new fanbase. Even if a one-year deal for Chisholm is valued at $20-plus million, he can afford it.”
The Angels have a fascinating outlook ahead with their new ownership, which clashes a decent amount with what their current team outlook feels like.
They’ve often been floated as a team that could trade experienced MLB players away, like shortstop Zach Neto.
But if the Angels go out and sign Chisholm, they’d certainly keep Neto to form a strong middle infield duo.
Why Yankees Would Let Jazz Chisholm Leave
For Chisholm to reach the Angels, of course, the Yankees would likely have to not offer him a reasonable new deal, because the second baseman has publicly seemed open to a return to the Bronx.
“I love it as a Yankee,” Chisholm said when the season ended.
Do they love him back?
“The Yankees have seemed ready to move on from Chisholm for months, and they have two potential replacements at second base in Anthony Volpe and Luis García Jr.,” Rymer writes.
The Yankees could certainly decide to just load up on talent and make it fit, but they may also choose to let Chisholm walk and focus their resources elsewhere.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees predicted to lose Jazz Chisholm Jr. to AL West team in free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. made it clear. He prefers to stay with the New York Yankees.
"This is where I want to be. I love it as a Yankee," Chisholm said after New York's loss in Game 3 of the ALDS.
However, do the Yankees want to retain Chisholm? They could replace him at second base with Anthony Volpe.
Or the AL East club could move Luis Garcia Jr. back to middle infield and hope Ben Rice improves defensively at first base.
Regardless, Chisholm may be headed elsewhere this winter. Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer predicts that the two-time All-Star will sign with the Los Angeles Angels.
"The Angels are just one of many teams that would have to be interested in such a deal. They are in need of help at the keystone, specifically, and upside on offense, generally. Chisholm can provide both, and some energy to boot," Rymer wrote.
Los Angeles could use another All-Star potential player or two in the lineup, and Chisholm is a consistent threat to hit 30 home runs and steal 30 bases a year.
He fell short of his expectations in 2026, hitting 19 homers with 41 steals after saying he wanted to have a 50-50 year.
If the Yankees are moving on from Chisholm, the Angels are a reasonable landing spot for the left-handed hitter.
"Depending on when the sale is finalized, signing Chisholm would also be a relatively low-risk way for Stan Kroenke to ingratiate himself with his new fanbase," Rymer added. "Even if a one-year deal for Chisholm is valued at $20-plus million, he can afford it."
Could this be the end of Chisholm's tenure in New York?

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Blue Jays linked to Yankees All-Star ahead of MLB offseason
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers
item.description: The MLB offseason could be a wild one, especially if there is a work stoppage, and the Toronto Blue Jays could be looking for ways to add more offense before it happens. YES of NO: Jazz Chisholm Jr. to the Blue Jays? Mark Feinsand lists Toronto as one of the potential suitors for the Yankees second baseman. https://t.co/UOFyNznsee — SleeperBlueJays (@SleeperBlueJays) October 12, 2026 One intriguing possibility involves New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., with MLB.com's Mark Feinsa
item.content:encoded:
The MLB offseason could be a wild one, especially if there is a work stoppage, and the Toronto Blue Jays could be looking for ways to add more offense before it happens.
YES of NO: Jazz Chisholm Jr. to the Blue Jays? Mark Feinsand lists Toronto as one of the potential suitors for the Yankees second baseman. https://t.co/UOFyNznsee
— SleeperBlueJays (@SleeperBlueJays) October 12, 2026
One intriguing possibility involves New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., with MLB.com's Mark Feinsand identifying Toronto as a potential landing spot for the two-time All-Star.
Why Chisholm could make sense for Toronto
Jul 19, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) and center fielder Trent Grisham (12) celebrate after defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
There is an obvious argument for the Blue Jays pursuing Chisholm. Toronto finished last in MLB in runs scored in 2026, producing only 648 runs. Adding a dynamic left-handed hitter with Chisholm's power and speed could give the lineup a much-needed jolt.
Chisholm did not duplicate his 2025 production, when he became a 30-30 player, but he still provided plenty of value in 2026. He hit .231 with 19 home runs, 55 RBIs and 41 stolen bases over 137 games while producing 3.5 fWAR. His 41 stolen bases ranked third in the American League.
The Blue Jays also have a potential opening at second base. Ernie Clement can handle the position, but Feinsand noted that Clement struggled significantly down the stretch, posting a .442 OPS across August and September. Toronto general manager Ross Atkins has also indicated that Clement will have to earn his starting role next spring.
That could create an opportunity for Chisholm to step into the lineup while allowing Clement to take on a valuable super-utility role.
Why Toronto should think twice
Mar 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) slides safely into third base against the San Francisco Giants in the second inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images
The biggest question is whether Chisholm would be worth the financial commitment required to bring him to Toronto.
Despite his talent, the 29-year-old is coming off a down offensive season. He struck out 157 times in 532 plate appearances and posted a 29.5% strikeout rate, placing him in the bottom 10% of MLB in that category. His 30.9% whiff rate also ranked in the bottom 10%.
Additionally, there are questions about his injury history and how much money Toronto should commit to him following a season in which his offensive production declined.
Feinsand's analysis suggests a three-to-four-year contract worth roughly $20 million annually could be a reasonable range, although the final price will depend heavily on how the free-agent market develops.
For Toronto, the upside is obvious: Chisholm brings speed, athleticism, power and a left-handed bat to a lineup that badly needs more production.
The risk is equally clear.

item.content:encoded:
Should the New York Yankees consider making a blockbuster trade for San Francisco Giants‘ infielder Matt Chapman?
After a disappointing 2026 season that concluded with an early exit in the MLB playoffs, the offseason is now for the Yanks.
Entering the offseason, the expectation is that the Yankees will look a lot different in certain areas of the diamond. One of those areas could be third base, where the Yankees really struggled offensively in 2026.
Matt Chapman stands out as a possible trade candidate, and a player New York should consider trading for.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Urged to Part Ways with 7X MLB All-Star in Offseason Move
Yankees Trade Package for Matt Chapman Revealed
In this hypothetical trade package, the New York Yankees land Giants’ $151 million infielder Matt Chapman for two players: RHP Clarke Schmidt and LHP prospect Kyle Carr.
Recently, BR.com’s Joel Reuter named Matt Chapman as one of 25 possible offseason trade candidates, and with the Yankees’ need for a left side of the field player, rumors are likely to spin in for the Yankees to acquire Chapman.
“While Rafael Devers, Willy Adames and Jung Hoo Lee are generally viewed as unavailable or immovable, Chapman is the one high-priced veteran the Giants might be able to flip, using last year’s Nolan Arenado trade as a blueprint of sorts. He had season-ending core muscle and hernia surgery in August, but is expected to be ready for the start of next season.”
In 2026, Chapman hit 7 home runs, 18 doubles, and posted an OPS+ of 97 in 84 games.
Injuries were clearly part of Chapman’s 2026 season, but that shouldn’t stop the Yankees from acquiring a consistent Gold Glove shortstop, and considering Clarke Schmidt doesn’t really have a role in the Yankees’ rotation, he could be expendable.
Chapman is tied to a six-year, $151 million contract, but he’s consistently been a 4.0+ bWAR player, which makes the contract a reasonable one to take on. His bWAR was 2.7 in 2026, but in only 84 games, that’s a very solid number. For comparison, Ryan McMahon (the Yankees’ primary third baseman) posted a bWAR of 0.0 in 124 games played.
More MLB on Heavy: Dave Roberts Sounds Off on Will Smith After Brewers Loss

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] New York Yankees Urged to Part Ways with 7X MLB All-Star in Offseason Move

item.description: Decisions, decisions. For the New York Yankees this offseason, the front office has several decisions to make regarding retaining players who are set to hit the open market in free agency. One of those big decisions for Brian Cashman and company is with 7X MLB All-Star infielder Paul Goldschmidt, who has indicated he would like to play in the 2027 season, but will it be with the New York Yankees?
