item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees enter the offseason with nine arbitration-eligible players projected to cost a combined $36.7 million in 2027, according to MLB Trade Rumors' Matt Swartz, who creates the projections on an annual basis.
But the Yankees could hold on to some of that money by nontendering — that is, declining to offer contracts — to some players.
Two injured pitchers, Clarke Schmidt and Fernando Cruz, are the realistic nontender candidates. Cutting both would trim $6.8 million from the bill.
| NEW YORK YANKEES — PROJECTED 2027 ARBITRATION SALARIES (9 PLAYERS) | | |
| Player | Service Time | Projected Salary |
| Clarke Schmidt | 5.148 | $4.5 million |
| Luis García Jr. | 5.142 | $11 million |
| Ryan Weathers | 4.066 | $3.1 million |
| Fernando Cruz | 4.035 | $2.3 million |
| José Caballero | 3.170 | $3.7 million |
| Anthony Volpe | 3.142 | $4 million |
| Luis Gil | 3.119 | $2.3 million |
| Heliot Ramos | 3.103 | $3.2 million |
| Austin Wells | 3.031 | $2.6 million |
| Source: MLB Trade Rumors, "Projected Arbitration Salaries For 2027" — mlbtraderumors.com | | |
Luis García Jr. Tops New York Yankees Arbitration Projections
Luis García Jr. is the lone double-digit case at a projection of $11 million, in his last arbitration year before free agency. He hit .277/.309/.521 with 30 homers and 92 RBI in 147 games between the Nationals and the Yankees, a career year, according to ESPN season statistics.
Anthony Volpe climbs from $3.475 million to a projected $4 million after playing only 70 games. He batted .245/.321/.336 with two homers, 28 RBI and 12 steals, an 88 wRC+ in 234 plate appearances, according to StatMuse's player page for Volpe. The projection reflects his prior platform season and remaining control rather than a full year of work.
He returned in September as a utility infielder after Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s injury and got a look at third base, according to MLB Trade Rumors on Volpe at third.
José Caballero jumps from $2 million to $3.7 million as a Super Two, a designation that allows certain players to enter arbitration a year early — after two years instead of three. Caballero hit .231/.290/.365 with 14 homers and 34 steals in 136 games, fifth in the American League in steals, with an 83 wRC+, according to CBS Sports player page for Caballero.
Ryan Weathers, acquired from the Miami Marlins in January, projects at $3.1 million after 25 starts, 137.1 innings and a 3.60 ERA. He landed on the injured list late in the season with a forearm strain.
Luis Gil lands at $2.3 million, barely above his $2.1625 million salary, after a 4.61 ERA and a 7.13 FIP across 27.1 innings in nine appearances, four of them starts. Heliot Ramos, acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the deadline, is a first-timer projected at $3.2 million after hitting .243/.303/.408 with 13 homers in 112 games, then .198/.309/.379 in 38 games following the trade. Austin Wells, also a first-time arbitration candidate, checks in at $2.6 million with three more years of control.
Fernando Cruz and Clarke Schmidt Face Non-Tender Decisions
Cruz, 36, went on the 60-day injured list in late August with a partial UCL tear and chose rest over surgery, according to CBS Sports. His 3.13 ERA in 54.2 innings came with 67 strikeouts, 32 walks and a 4.18 FIP, walking 5.3 batters per nine innings. Nontendering him saves the full $2.3 million.
Schmidt is projected at $4.5 million, identical to his 2026 salary, after Tommy John surgery in June 2025 and a biceps neuritis shutdown, according to MLB Trade Rumors on Schmidt's injured list placement. The pitcher posted a 3.85 ERA over 323 innings from 2023 to 2025. The projected 2027 staff already lists Fried, Schlittler, Cole, Rodón, Warren, Weathers and Carlos Lagrange, and Schmidt cannot be optioned. Nontendering him saves $4.5 million.
Cruz alone leaves $34.4 million on the books. Schmidt alone leaves $32.2 million. Both exits leave $29.9 million for the other seven.
A pre-deadline deal with either pitcher, the other route for borderline cases, would save less than a full nontender.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — If the Yankees can keep their stuff together (i.e. they don’t screw up bunt plays and other baseball nuances), it says here they get past this dynamic Rays team. And if the Yankees can do that, they have the next best thing to a bye on their path to the World Series: an American League Central opponent.
The Yankees rolled past the Red Sox like they were playing a bunch of computer nerds, which in effect they may have been (see comments from Boston slugger Willson Contreras). Most vitally, the Yankees’ vaunted rotation is as sound and superb as any going.




Access the Yankees beat like never before

Don’t miss Greg Joyce’s text messages from The Bronx and beyond — he’s giving Sports+ subscribers the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Sign Up Now
The Yankees are in such fine pitching shape they’re bypassing an opportunity in Game 1 of the AL Division Series here to employ the red-hot Carlos Rodón, the AL’s second-hottest starter behind Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, in place of future Hall of Famer Gerrit Cole. I’d have gone with Rodón and his revitalized slider myself, but then, I don’t have to explain my opinions to the Cooperstown-bound Cole.
Nothing against Cole (except the nine homers he’s allowed in his last four starts), but Rodón’s ERA since returning is 1.89 and his batting average against is an MLB-best .146. Plus, the Rays aren’t nearly as great against lefties (.679 OPS vs. .746 vs. righties), and Rodón completely shut them down (two hits, eight strikeouts) over eight innings 10 days ago.

item.content:encoded:
Will Aaron Judge Be Available For Yankees' ALDS Series vs. Rays?
The New York Yankees surged its way to the American League Division Series after its two-game sweep over the Boston Red Sox. And yet, the Yankees' dominant series win came without star Aaron Judge.
Judge has been out with a calf strain injury since Sept. 19, when the Yankees originally moved him to the 10-day injured list. Especially as the Yankees creep towards its next postseason series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Judge's timeline and likeliness of making the 26-man roster this weekend is still unknown.
The Yankees have until Saturday morning to submit their final rosters ahead of Game 1 at 6:30 p.m. in St. Petersburg, Florida. If Judge were to be added to the roster, it would be his first roster appearance this postseason run for New York.
Manager Aaron Boone provided clarity on Judge ahead of submitting the roster, and gave a status update on Judge’s health.
"The trainers will obviously play a big part in this. As the day unfolds, we'll see where we're at and what it potentially looks like for the series," Boone said.
Although Judge has been a part of live batting practice, Boone is still weighing in how, and when, Judge can be utilized against the Rays.
"It's just as far as him and the field, potentially," Boone said. "But we're looking at the days and so it's more, 'Is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player?' That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days having taken live [batting practice]."
The Yankees' postseason run continues tomorrow at 6:30 p.m. in a three-game divisional series against the Rays.

He's doing more today over at [Steinbrenner Field in Tampa] and [Tropicana Field]. So we'll probably make those calls later tonight." Asked if Judge had run the bases during his wo
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's status for the New York Yankees' American League Division Series matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays is still uncertain, manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Friday.
"We'll see," Boone said when asked about Judge's availability. "He'll be working out [Friday]. He hit again live [Thursday] at Yankee Stadium. He's doing more today over at [Steinbrenner Field in Tampa] and [Tropicana Field]. So we'll probably make those calls later tonight."
Asked if Judge had run the bases during his workouts, Boone said he wasn't sure but knew that Judge had been running.
The Yankees have until 10 a.m. ET Saturday morning to submit their 26-player roster for Game 1, which is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. ET in Tampa Bay.
Aaron Boone gives an update on Aaron Judge's status for the ALDS: "We'll see. He'll be working out today, hit again live yesterday."
Boone is not sure if Judge has run the bases but knows that Judge has started running pic.twitter.com/RItnaCMlAj
— SNY Yankees (@snyyankees) October 2, 2026
Judge hasn't played since suffering a calf injury on Sept. 16 and was placed on the injured list two days later. He was left off the Yankees' roster during their wild-card series versus the Boston Red Sox — though the Yankees didn't need Judge in their two-game sweep, winning by scores of 9-0 and 9-2.
One consideration in playing Judge at Tropicana Field is the ballpark's artificial turf. That could preclude him from playing the outfield if he's on the roster.
"It plays into it a little bit," Boone said, via the Associated Press. "But we're looking at the days and so it's more is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player? That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days having taken live BP."
Games 1 and 2 at Tropicana Field are scheduled for Saturday and Monday. The series shifts to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday and Game 4, if necessary, on Thursday, if the preference was to save Judge for the grass field in New York. Game 5 at Tampa Bay is scheduled for Oct. 10.
The Yankees could decide to have Judge on the ALDS roster even if he's only available to pinch-hit. If he can't play in right field, Ben Rice will likely remain at designated hitter. He batted 5-for-9 with 2 home runs and 6 RBI in the two wild-card games.
However, Rays manager Kevin Cash is proceeding as if Judge will be in the Yankees' lineup.
"I expect him playing right field, hitting third," Cash said, via the AP.
Gerrit Cole (3.61 ERA) will be the Yankees' starting pitcher for Game 1, while Drew Rasmussen (2.67 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays.

item.content:encoded:
New Aaron Judge Rumors, Updated Injury Status for Yankees vs. Rays in 2026 MLB Playoffs
The Tampa Bay Rays may have to wait until closer to Saturday's first pitch of the ALDS to find out if Game 1 starter Drew Rasmussen will be facing Aaron Judge at the plate.
ESPN's Jeff Passan reported earlier on Friday that Judge's status "remains up in the air and is unlikely to be decided until shortly before the series begins Saturday, sources familiar with the deliberations told ESPN."
"Some in the organization want him to play," Passan reported. "Others, wary of him further aggravating the injury and imperiling him for the remainder of the postseason, would prefer to wait another week."
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters that Judge could be included on the roster even if he is not in the lineup for Game 1:
Passan noted the decision is also impacted by the fact Judge could be returning as a designated hitter. Notably, DH Luis García Jr. just helped the Yankees close out their Wild Card sweep of the Boston Red Sox by opening Game 2 scoring with a home run.
Judge initially said he hoped to return for the beginning of the postseason before he was left off the Yankees' Wild Card roster amid his recovery from the right calf strain that resulted in a trip to the injured list on Sept. 19.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said at the time the decision was made because the club didn't feel Judge was "all the way back."
Judge has appeared in just seven games for the Yankees since he was shut down with a right rib injury May 31. Following his return Sept. 8, he was held to a batting average of .174 with one home run in 24 plate appearances before suffering the calf injury.
The Yankees will hope giving Judge more time to recover from his latest injury will result in a more productive return from the slugger. Should he sit out the divisional series, he would gain an additional week to recover in the event the Yankees advance to the ALCS.
Gerrit Cole will start Game 1 for the Yankees when the ALDS begins Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET in St. Petersburg. He will be facing a more rested lineup given that the Rays sat out the Wild Card round after clinching the AL's top seed.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will play the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series.
Game 1 of the series will begin at 6:30 p.m. EDT on Friday at Tropicana Field.
The Yankees were without star outfielder Aaron Judge in the American League Wild Card Series due to a calf strain.
Despite Judge's absence, the Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox 2-0 in the Wild Card Series. New York outscored Boston 18-2.
Before the ALDS, Yankees manager Aaron Boone announced an update on Judge.
New York Yankees' Aaron Boone Announces Aaron Judge News Before ALDS vs. Rays
Aaron Boone gives an update on Aaron Judge's status for the ALDS: "We'll see. He'll be working out today, hit again live yesterday."
Boone is not sure if Judge has run the bases but knows that Judge has started running
Aaron Boone gives an update on Aaron Judge's status for the ALDS: "We'll see. He'll be working out today, hit again live yesterday."Boone is not sure if Judge has run the bases but knows that Judge has started running pic.twitter.com/RItnaCMlAj— SNY Yankees (@snyyankees) October 2, 2026
Looking at Aaron Judge
The Yankees placed Judge on the injured list on Sept. 19 with a right calf strain.
Judge missed most of the season with a right rib stress fracture, landing him on the IL on June 2. New York activated him on Sept. 7.
Before being placed on the IL in June, Judge hit .248/.375/.533 with 17 home runs and 38 RBI over 59 games this season.
Judge struggled after returning from the IL in Sept., hitting just .190/.227/.333 with one home run and three RBI over six games before landing on the IL again.
Since making his MLB debut in 2016, Judge has slashed 291/.410/.610 with 386 home runs and 871 RBI.
Judge has won three AL MVP Awards throughout his career.
Looking at the Yankees-Rays ALDS
Here is the Yankees-Rays ALDS schedule:
- Game 1: 6:30 p.m. EDT on Saturday, Oct. 3, @ Tropicana Field
- Game 2: 8:00 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 5, @ Tropicana Field
- Game 3: 8:00 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, Oct. 7, @ Yankee Stadium
- Game 4 (if necessary): 8:00 p.m. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 8, @ Yankee Stadium
- Game 5 (if necessary): 8:00 p.m. EDT on Saturday, Oct. 10, @ Tropicana Field
All of the games will be available to watch on TBS and HBO Max.
The winner of the Yankees-Rays series will play the winner of the ALDS between the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians in the American League Championship Series.
The Rays finished the season with the best record in the American League at 98-64.
The Yankees ended the regular season 4 1/2 games behind the Rays for first place in the division.
The Rays won seven of 13 games against the Yankees this season. However, the Yankees won three of four games in their last series with the Rays.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] 5 Reasons Why the Yankees Shouldn't Keep Aaron Judge off the ALDS Roster
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown

The Texas Rangers won the World Series by com
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees may have blown the doors off the Boston Red Sox without Aaron Judge, but that doesn't mean that they don't need their captain. For anyone who watched this team all year—or even the past few years—the best version of this team has Judge in the lineup.
Who knows what would've happened to the division this year if Judge were healthy, or, in the case of the 2023 season, their postseason chances if Dodger Stadium hadn't taken him out. The Texas Rangers won the World Series by coming out of the American League, but the Yankees took a series from them without Judge that summer.
Heading into the division series against Tampa Bay, the Yankees should activate him if he's healthy enough to play. Here are five reasons why.
Lineup protection
The Yankees' lineup outscored the Red Sox 18-2 in two games. It's hard to find a bigger mismatch in the postseason than that with the remaining teams.
As great as Ben Rice performed, imagine a world where a pitcher is staring at who is coming up, and the part of the lineup he has to navigate is Judge, Rice, and Cody Bellinger. They'll be extra careful and may be forced to pitch to these guys because, as Bellinger proved in Game 2, if you put runners on in front of him, he has a shot at taking a pitcher deep.
Still a homer threat even if he struggles
Judge struggled throughout the 2024 postseason. However, one of the memorable home runs during that series came off him, taking Emmanuel Clase deep. The Yankees still lost that game, but it showed that as long as Judge is in that lineup, he can change the complexion of any game.
At that point, Clase was one of baseball's best closers. Judge still sent a triple-digit pitch into the seats.
Flexibility proved to be a little overrated in the Wild Card Series
Aaron Boone mixed and matched his roster a bit in the Wild Card Series, but not everyone performed despite the run parade. Amed Rosario and Heliot Ramos, specifically, provided next to nothing. Ramos is essentially Judge's replacement on the roster when the Yankees face lefties, and the southpaw Payton Tolle overpowered him in Game 1.
Judge may not have fared much better than Ramos, but there's a difference between a bench bat and a three-time MVP. Pitchers are looking at that matchup a little differently.
The best defensive roster has Judge in right field
Judge has a calf strain, and playing on it could be detrimental. But if a doctor says he's healthy enough to get out there, he should be in right field. With Judge in the outfield, that opens up the DH slot so Ben Rice and Luis Garcia Jr. can play at the same time. The best Yankee lineup has those three in there at the same time.
No "what ifs"
The 2026 season has been one big "What if?" What if the Yankees were healthy? What if the rotation didn't deal with as many IL stints as it did? What if Judge stayed on the field?
There's no remedying what happened in the regular season, but if Judge is healthy and can go up against the Rays, the Yankees can put a lot of those questions to rest — especially if they beat Tampa with Judge's help.
Anyone who thought the Yankees would have won the AL East if Judge had stayed on the field would be somewhat redeemed. Granted, the stakes are a little higher than what happens between April and September.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
Why Cam Schlittler's 8-word truth bomb will have Yankees fans feeling confident for Rays series appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Is this finally the year the New York Yankees get it together? For years, the Bronx has seen their baseball team make it to the postseason, only to falter in the biggest moments. This year, New York is once again one of the top teams left, despite being a Wild Card team.
The Yankees are up against a truly formidable foe in the first-seeded Tampa Bay Rays. There's a lot of concern about whether this veteran team can go toe-to-toe with their resurgent division rivals. However, ace Cam Schlittler isn't worried about his team in the slightest. Why? Well, here's what the star has to say.
"We're on a roll at the right time," Schlittler said, per Gary Phillips.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Aaron Boone further expanded on that point, saying, "I like the balance of our club right now. Again, we played great baseball in a lot of ways here, obviously anchored by our two great starters that got us off on a great foot. But a lot of really good things happened with this group. We get a chance to keep it going."
The Yankees are coming off a comfortable dismantling of the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card round. Schlitter got the start in Game 1, and the ace pitcher immediately showed why he's earned his spot as the postseason opening starter. Schlittler pitches 6 1/3 innings of no-run ball, allowing just two hits while striking out ten batters. The Yankees bullpen finished the job, holding Boston scoreless as their hitting unit scored nine runs.
Max Fried got the ball in Game 2, and he was also incredible for New York. In six innings, the Yankees star allowed just one hit while striking out six. New York cruised to a comfortable 9-2 win to secure their spot in the Wild Card round. They now look to keep that momentum against a well-rested Rays team.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees' Aaron Judge reveals early injury status for ALDS against Rays originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees did exactly what they had to do on both sides of the baseball against the Boston Red Sox in the American League Wild Card series.
As the Yankees prepare for the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays, there's reason to believe this roster will be even better than it was during the Wild Card.
As of now, it remains uncertain what the Yankees want to do with Aaron Judge, or whether he can even play, but there's hope around the fan base that he might come back.
Speaking to reporters while celebrating his team advancing, Judge said that he feels good, but he doesn't have an answer as to whether he's eventually playing.
"We just finished the Wild Card," Judge said in the middle of a clubhouse celebration, per NJ.com. "We'll get into that as we get close. I got nothing for you yet, but I have an opportunity to get ready. That's what I've been doing every day."
"I'm feeling good," he said.
Getting Judge back has to be the biggest priority for the Yankees over this postseason.
While the Yankees played very well against the Red Sox and there was a lot to like, things are only going to get more difficult.
Not having the best hitter in Major League Baseball doesn't help, and the Yankees will have to work around it if he's not ready to go.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Aaron Judge says quiet part out loud about Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees are riding high after defeating the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series on Thursday. Now they will face their other division rival, the Tampa Bay Rays, in the ALDS beginning on Saturday, Oct. 3, at Tropicana Field.
Going into the series, Aaron Judge was highly complimentary of the Rays, per Gary Phillips of The New York Daily News. Essentially, Judge said that the Rays are a complete team, but that the Yankees are ready to take them on.
"They got everything," Judge said. "We're up for the task."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The Rays have a vast array of assets working in their favor. They won the AL East Division with a 98-64 record. They also went 55-26 at home and defeated the Yankees 7-6 throughout the season.
The Rays also have power at the plate with Junior Caminero, who hit 42 home runs. They have consistency at the plate in Yandy Díaz, who led the AL in hits with 180. Additionally, Chandler Simpson is a reliable presence on the base paths.
Nevertheless, the Yankees have a lot going for them. They dominated the Red Sox with 9-0 and 9-2 victories in the Wild Card series. Plus, their staff ace Cam Schlittler is on a roll after pitching 6 1/3 scoreless innings against Boston. Their bullpen, led by Carlos Rodón, is also pretty top-notch.
The Yankees also lead the AL with a 3.24 ERA.
Meanwhile, Judge was left off the roster for the Wild Card series because of a recent calf strain. His status for the ALDS remains unknown.

item.content:encoded:
El veterano derecho Gerrit Cole abrirá el Juego 1 de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana por los Yankees contra los Rays el sábado en el Tropicana Field, anunció el club en la mañana del viernes.
Cole estaba programado para abrir el Juego 3 de la Serie del Comodín de la L.A. contra los Medias Rojas, pero Nueva York despachó a Boston mediante una barrida de dos juegos.
El lanzador de 36 años dejó marca de 10-9 con efectividad de 3.61 en 22 aperturas esta temporada, luego de perderse todo el año pasado debido a una cirugía Tommy John. Cole registró 131 ponches en 127 entradas lanzadas tras hacer su debut de temporada en el Yankee Stadium el 22 de mayo.
Esta será la 23ra presentación en postemporada en la carrera de Cole -- todas como abridor -- y su primera desde el Juego 5 de la Serie Mundial del 2024, cuando permitió cinco carreras sucias en 6.2 episodios en una derrota que puso fin a la serie. Ha dejado un promedio de carreras limpias de 2.93 en 12 aperturas de playoffs de por vida con los Yankees.
Cole se enfrentará al derecho de los Rays, Drew Rasmussen, un dos veces convocado al Juego de Estrellas cuya efectividad de 2.67 fue la séptima más baja entre los lanzadores abridores calificados en el 2026.
Cole realizó tres aperturas esta campaña contra Tampa Bay, permitiendo tres carreras o menos en las tres salidas. Posee efectividad de 3.33 en 23 aperturas de por vida frente a los Rays, su mayor cantidad contra cualquier equipo. Cole también se ha medido a Tampa Bay cuatro veces en la postemporada, incluyendo dos en la SDLA del 2020.

item.title: [Yahoo] Yankees Banking on Track Record By Turning to Gerrit Cole In Game 1 of ALDS
item.dc:creator: Ben Watanabe
item.description: Through all the hand-wringing over the lineup and injury status of Aaron Judge all season, the fact of the matter was that the New York Yankees possess an embarrassment of riches in their starting rotation. It ultimately might be what delivers them another World Series. So the fact that the Yankees could turn to arguably their fourth-best starting pitcher for Game 1 of their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, and only prompt minor debate among observers about the move, i
item.content:encoded:
Through all the hand-wringing over the lineup and injury status of Aaron Judge all season, the fact of the matter was that the New York Yankees possess an embarrassment of riches in their starting rotation. It ultimately might be what delivers them another World Series.
So the fact that the Yankees could turn to arguably their fourth-best starting pitcher for Game 1 of their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, and only prompt minor debate among observers about the move, is another sign of how stacked the team is on the mound.
Gerrit Cole will start Game 1, the Yankees announced Friday morning, going with the safe choice to open the series. The Rays will counter with All-Star right-hander Drew Rasmussen.
Cole comes into Saturday's game with plenty of rest. He was scheduled to start Game 3 on Thursday against the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series, but that game turned out not to be necessary. The 36-year-old last pitched more than a week ago, giving up two runs in 5 2/3 innings against these same Rays on Sept. 23.
Carlos Rodon also has plenty of rest, however, and even ace Cam Schlittler should be relatively fresh, having not pitched since Game 1 against the Red Sox on Tuesday. Rodon, Schlittler and Max Fried all have better numbers this season than Cole, who missed all of last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery. But Cole has the name and the track record.
Cole has started 12 playoff games in his Yankees career, with a 2.93 ERA. He's started 22 playoff games in total with a 2.77 ERA and 1.020 WHIP that reveal how misleading his 7-8 career postseason record is.
Going solely by this season, the Yankees might have better options. But Cole has the longest resume of success, and on Saturday, he'll have the ball.

item.content:encoded:
Gerrit Cole abrirá por los Yankees de Nueva York contra Drew Rasmussen y los Rays de Tampa en el primer juego de la serie divisional de la Liga Americana la noche del sábado.
Cole estaba previsto para abrir el tercer partido de la serie de comodines contra Boston el jueves, pero los Yankees barrieron a su rival de división. El derecho de 36 años, seis veces All-Star, terminó 10-9 con una efectividad de 3.61 en 22 aperturas esta temporada tras recuperarse de una cirugía Tommy John que lo obligó a perderse la temporada 2025.
Rasmussen terminó 16-5 con una efectividad de 2.67 para los Rays y fue seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas por segunda temporada consecutiva. El derecho de 31 años se sometió dos veces en la universidad a cirugías por un ligamento desgarrado en el codo y necesitó un procedimiento de refuerzo interno en julio de 2023 que lo obligó a perderse más de un año.
Tiene marca de 5-2 con una efectividad de 1.81 en 10 aperturas y una aparición como relevista contra los Yankees, con 70 ponches en 59 innings y dos tercios.
Tampa Bay lideró la Liga Americana con 98 victorias, lo que le valió un pase directo y la ventaja de local en el renovado Tropicana Field. Tuvieron que disputar sus juegos como locales de 2025 al otro lado de la bahía, en Tampa, en el Steinbrenner Field, la sede de los entrenamientos de primavera de los Yankees, tras los daños sufridos por el Trop a causa del huracán Milton el 9 de octubre de 2024.
Los Rays no han ganado una serie de postemporada desde 2020, cuando perdieron la Serie Mundial ante los Los Angeles Dodgers. Vencieron a los Yankees 3-2 en la Serie Divisional y conquistaron el segundo banderín de la franquicia.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] An open letter to Yankees fans who wanted Brian Cashman and Aaron Boone gone | Klapisch
item.dc:creator: Bob Klapisch
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — This is an open letter to anyone who's railed against Brian Cashman and Aaron Boone over the years. That's a huge swath of Yankees fans – maybe all of them. So let's call this a mass mailing. The Yankees are a step closer to the World Series for two reasons. The first was the Red Sox's glaring deficits. Scoring just two runs in 18 innings, they just weren't good enough to hang with the Yankees. If the Wild Card Series were replayed 10 times, the Yankees would likely win ni
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — This is an open letter to anyone who's railed against Brian Cashman and Aaron Boone over the years. That's a huge swath of Yankees fans – maybe all of them. So let's call this a mass mailing.
The Yankees are a step closer to the World Series for two reasons. The first was the Red Sox's glaring deficits. Scoring just two runs in 18 innings, they just weren't good enough to hang with the Yankees. If the Wild Card Series were replayed 10 times, the Yankees would likely win nine.
The second reason is why we're here today. Although this isn't the greatest Yankees roster of the last 20 years, it is remarkably well-constructed and well-managed. That's another way of saying Cashman and Boone have done their jobs well. They deserve credit for that.
The question is whether the critics will ever reconsider. I have my doubts. The folks who've been demanding Cashman's and Boone's firing for almost a decade aren't exactly open to reasonable dialogue. They're dug in so deep that one of them, who just happens to be an old college buddy, insisted, "Anyone could've beaten the Red Sox. That's how much they sucked."
My friend isn't entirely wrong — at least about Boston's non-existent offense. It's hard to believe this was the same team that went on a 14-game winning streak this summer.
But to suggest that any manager with Cam Schlittler as their ace and Ben Rice hitting lasers could've taken down the Sox is flat-out wrong. That's like saying all managers are the same. Their only job is to fill out the lineup card and talk to the TV cameras after the game.
Not quite.
Managers have personality traits that can enhance the roster's potential. Joe Torre, laid-back in a streetwise sort of way, was the perfect candidate to replace the hyper-involved Buck Showalter. Torre was never loud, but still tough enough to absorb late owner George Steinbrenner's manic behavior.
When Torre's enthusiasm for managing waned by 2006, Joe Girardi — ultra-prepared, obsessed with process — represented the pendulum swinging in the other direction. And when the next generation of Yankees decided Girardi was just too uptight and disconnected from the clubhouse, Boone won over Cashman because he was smart, calm and relatable.
I realize fans no longer care about Boone's personality. Not even his .582 winning percentage — second only to the Dodgers' Dave Roberts among active managers — gets the credit it deserves. What matters are championships. Boone has none since he replaced Girardi in 2018. In the Bronx, that's 0-for-forever.
That doesn't mean Boone is a bad manager. He checks so many other boxes that have kept the Yankees competitive. The players like Boone, but more importantly, they trust his instincts. In fact, Boone had a terrific series against Boston, embarrassing Chad Tracy, his counterpart in the other dugout.
Boone didn't make any significant mistakes against the Sox. His most important decision of the series came in Game 1.
After allowing Schlittler to throw 117 pitches, Boone summoned Paul Blackburn in the seventh inning to protect a 2-0 lead. Facing Ceddanne Rafaela with the tying run at the plate, Blackburn induced an inning-ending double play. The Yankees went on to score seven runs in the next two innings.
Tracy, on the other hand, made two decisions that doomed Boston. In both games, he pulled his starter in the fifth inning with two outs and the Sox trailing 1-0 — first Payton Tolle, then Sonny Gray. The Yankees promptly destroyed reliever Erik Miller on both occasions.
Several Sox players, including Gray and Willson Contreras, have since second-guessed Tracy's strategy and the team's overall direction.
You don't hear that kind of anti-Boone sniping in the Yankees' clubhouse. Even Boone's handling of Aaron Judge's irritation at being left off the Wild Card roster showed finesse. Boone demonstrated he was in control without making a show of pulling rank.
One former Yankee texted me the other day about the back-and-forth between Boone and Judge. He believes the episode showed how much Boone has grown on the job.
"All (Boone) said was, 'We don't expect Judge to be back,'" the former Yankee said. "That's Boone's way of telling the rest of the players, 'It's time for you to step up. Don't sit here waiting for Judge to rescue you.' It was a positive message."
Of course, it takes the right kind of players to understand that. The Yankees are a stable group. Even Jose Caballero, who came to the Yankees with the reputation of being a rogue element, has fallen into line.
That's where Cashman comes in. He made one right call after another in assembling this 93-win roster. The bullpen is airtight; the gamble on trading for closer David Bednar has worked to perfection. The GM made the smart move by promoting George Lombard Jr. this summer instead of waiting until September or 2027. And the rotation, finally healthy, is the Yankees' best since 2009.
MORE BY BOB KLAPISCH
All it took was one more piece — Max Fried. His signing in free agency in 2025 had Cashman's fingerprints all over it.
Beat the Rays, and the Yankees are back in the AL Championship Series. Win there, and they're back in the World Series for the second time in three years. At that point, those haters just might admit Cashman and Boone had something to do with it.
I'm such a nice guy that I'll give my friend a chance to admit he was wrong all along.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees remain alive in the MLB playoffs and will begin the ALDS on Saturday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
There’s at least one thing that the Yanks don’t have, something that no team in the league has, that the Yankees could once claim to have: the greatest closer of all time.
Mariano Rivera is retired now, just a fan of the game rather than the guy coming out of the bullpen to slam the door shut.
Occasionally, though, Rivera stats will make their way onto social media and start trending. They’ll remind baseball fans just how good Rivera once was.
It’s worth appreciating, even now, because the postseason is the time of year when managers get super aggressive with their relief pitchers.
With other guys, it doesn’t always work.
With Rivera, it nearly always did.
Mariano Rivera Trending Record
One particular record of Rivera’s was shared recently on X (formerly Twitter) and proves just how remarkable he was in the postseason during a dominant era of Yankees baseball.
The stat was for “most postseason saves getting more than 3 outs.”
Rivera had 31 of them.
The next-closest pitcher had seven — that being Goose Gossage.
Four different guys had six such saves: Rollie Fingers, Dennis Eckersley, Kenley Jansen and Aroldis Chapman.
If you add up those five guys, they add up to the same amount of multi-inning saves that Rivera had all by himself.

5 Tug McGraw, Jason Motte pic.twitter.com/LI7Ms0KSbJ
— Codify (@CodifyBaseball) October 1, 2026
That way of sharing it that Codify Baseball used in that post really drives the point home.
How would anyone catch Rivera in this? It’s a bit of a niche stat, but it’s also about reliability and dominance. The Yankees could turn to ‘Mo’ and he would slam the door shut, no matter how early they had to bring him into the ballgame.
How It Applies This Season
One example stands out above the rest already this season.
In Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series between the Phillies and Braves, Philadelphia manager Don Mattingly brought his closer Jhoan Duran in to begin the seventh inning.
That did coincide with the top of Atlanta’s order, so Mattingly may not have planned on a three-inning save, but that’s certainly one possibility it set up for.
Duran never got to pitch the ninth, though. In the eighth, he gave up a go-ahead three-run homer to Austin Riley, and the Phillies went from leading to a loss. They dropped Game 3 two days later to be eliminated.
It just proved that not all relievers are capable of such multi-inning reliability as the kind Rivera brought to the table.
Rivera failed occasionally, yes, with nothing more painful than Game 7 of the 2001 World Series.
But the Yankees also won championships that they wouldn’t have won without Rivera. He was, and remains, one of one.

item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday night, the New York Yankees beat the Boston Red Sox by a score of 9-2.
With the victory, they swept the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series.
Bob Nightengale of USA Today wrote: “The New York Yankees sweep the Boston Red Sox out of the Bronx in humiliating fashion. They outscored the Red Sox 18-2 in the wild-card series. They are off to Tampa Bay for a best-of-five AL Division Series beginning Saturday”
Judge Makes Bellinger Statement After Sweep
Cody Bellinger finished the win with two hits, including one home run and four RBIs.
After the game, Aaron Judge was asked about Bellinger when he spoke to YES Network.
Meredith Marakovits: “Last night it was Ben Rice. Tonight it was Cody Bellinger with some big hits. Those two bats in the lineup. Just how valuable are they?”
Judge: “It’s amazing. We saw Ben Rice make a lot of strides last year. I knew coming into this year he’s going to have a great year for us. And then that’s why we signed back Cody Bellinger, man. He’s built for this. He’s built for New York. He’s built for the big moment. And he continues to show up for us when we need him.”
Looking At Bellinger
Bellinger is in the middle of his second season with the Yankees.
He has also spent time with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Chicago Cubs over 10 seasons at the MLB level.
As Judge alluded to, Bellinger signed a big deal with the Yankees over the offseason.
Looking At The Yankees
The Yankees finished the regular season as the second-place team in the American League East with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
They are looking to win their first World Series title since the 2009 season.

item.content:encoded:
Knicks' Josh Hart goes biblical on Cam Schlittler amid Yankees' postseason ride appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees took care of business without much fuss in their AL Wild Card series clash against the Boston Red Sox, sweeping the best-of-three with a run differential of +16. This domination would not have been possible without ace Cam Schlittler, who set the tone for the Yankees with a strong Game 1 start in which he shut out the Red Sox over 6.1 innings, striking out 10 while allowing just two hits and one walk — earning himself a huge fan in New York Knicks forward Josh Hart.
Hart, speaking to reporters on Thursday, waxed poetic when talking about the Yankees ace and went as far as to go biblical — saying that Schlittler might have his place alongside two deities in the throne of heaven.
"I'm very religious. I know Jesus is at God's right hand, but I think Cam Schlittler might be at his left. I'm excited, man," Hart said, via Ian Begley of SNY.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Josh Hart, noted Yankee fan, was asked if he has Yanks in 5 for the ALDS:
“I know Jesus is at God's right hand, but I think Cam Schlittler might be at his left,” he said.
Hart plans to attend Game 3 in The Bronx: pic.twitter.com/9uj16Z7jJg
— Ian Begley (@IanBegley) October 1, 2026
The Knicks forward said that he will be in attendance for Game 3 of the ALDS, when the series shifts from the Tampa Bay Rays' home at St. Petersburg to Yankee Stadium. Alas, Schlittler is currently penciled in to start for the Yankees in Game 2 of the ALDS on the road, so Hart won't be around to witness a performance from the purported "left-hand man" of God.
Schlittler continues to rise to the occasion for the Yankees, and as he showed last year, when he was still a rookie, that the postseason does not faze him whatsoever. In fact, Schlittler seems to perform better when the lights are at their brightest, and in adverse conditions.
In 2026, Schlittler has a better ERA on the road (1.16) than he has at home (2.86). Against the Rays this year, he has an ERA of 2.86 in 16.0 innings (three starts). He will once again be expected to work his magic for New York as they soldier on in their quest to win the franchise's 28th World Series title.
Related: Knicks' NBA-high family cost reveals the price of loyalty

item.title: [whec.com] Having bashed Boston without Judge, Yankees turn attention to AL Division Series vs. pesky Rays
item.dc:creator: Kiley Wren
item.description: Having bashed Boston without Judge, Yankees turn attention to AL Division Series vs. pesky Rays NEW YORK (AP) — Having bashed Boston without Aaron Judge, the New York Yankees face a far different task when they face the pesky Tampa Bay Rays in an AL Division Series starting Saturday, Riding powerful pitching led by Cam Schlitter and Max Fried, Yankees batters broke though just enough against Red Sox starters and beat up Boston’s bullpen in sweeping their rival in the Wild Card Series. “We’re goi
item.content:encoded:
Having bashed Boston without Judge, Yankees turn attention to AL Division Series vs. pesky Rays
NEW YORK (AP) — Having bashed Boston without Aaron Judge, the New York Yankees face a far different task when they face the pesky Tampa Bay Rays in an AL Division Series starting Saturday,
Riding powerful pitching led by Cam Schlitter and Max Fried, Yankees batters broke though just enough against Red Sox starters and beat up Boston’s bullpen in sweeping their rival in the Wild Card Series.
“We’re going to continue to rely on amazing starting pitching like we have all year,” Ben Rice said after Wednesday night’s 9-2 win. ”Especially in the postseason, that’s what you need.”
Schlittler and Fried combined to go 2-0 with a 0.73 ERA against the Red Sox with 16 strikeouts and two walks in 12 1/3 innings.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone must decide whether to open against the Rays with Gerrit Cole, who was set to start a Game 3 against Boston, or Carlos Rodón.
“Obviously, Gerrit’s lined up for that. Carlos is very much in play for that,” Boone said. “We have a ton of confidence in both guys. I think they’re both throwing the ball really well.”
Boone said it was possible Schlittler, Fried, Cole and Rodón all will start against the Rays. New York’s starters led the major leagues with a 3.30 ERA.
“That’s been the biggest strength for us throughout the year,” Boone said. “It sustained us. It got us through some difficult times. And I feel like they’re all in a good place right now.”
New York’s best-of-five series against the Rays has an extra off day between Games 1 and 2, allowing Schlittler to start the second game and come back on normal rest for a Game 5.
Whether Judge will return to the lineup remains unclear.
Sidelined since Sept. 16 by a strained right calf, Judge has resumed hitting.
“Saturday’s a long ways away, but I’m doing everything I can, all morning, night, during the game, everything to prepare myself to be ready to go,” Judge said. “So I want to be in there. So we’ll see what happens.”
Tampa Bay won the season series 7-6 en route to an AL-best 98-64 record, their runners often spinning around the bases like a roulette ball going around the wheel. The Rays were sixth in the major leagues with a .326 on-base percentage and tied for second with 164 stolen bases.
Rays batters struck out the fewest times in the major leagues at 1,145, an average of about two per game fewer than the Yankees.
Because they won the AL East and had a bye, the Rays will enter the series with five days’ rest — which some in baseball is convinced causes rust.
“The alternative is playing three must-win games or two out of three. I’ll take where we’re at,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said.
Rays left-handed pitchers held lefty batters to a .205 average during the regular season. Yankees lefty batters hit .500 (11 for 22) against Boston southpaws.
“They faced so many guys for months there where we were very left-handed, where in the fifth inning every day it was one lefty and then another one because that’s how they attack us,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. “So I’d like to think some of that familiarity and reps and all that prepared us well.”
New York was second in the majors with 223 home runs, three behind Houston. What was often a home-run-or-bust batting order diversified in the Wild Card Series.
Homegrown players — Rice, Spencer Jones, George Lombard Jr., Anthony Volpe and Austin Wells — combined for 11 RBIs.
“The young guys have done a tremendous job,” outfielder Cody Bellinger said. “It’s been fun to watch. It’s fun to watch them grow and they’ve been a huge part of our success.”
___

Sidelined since Sept. 16 by a strained right calf, Judge went to the Yankees’ Double-A ballpark in Somerset, New Jersey, for live batting practice Wednesday as he tries to work his way back from a leg injury to be available later in the postseason. “Satur
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge remains unsure for ALDS after missing Yankees’ first-round win over Red Sox
NEW YORK (AP) — Yankees captain Aaron Judge remained unsure of his Division Series status following New York’s Wild Card Series sweep of the Boston Red Sox.
Sidelined since Sept. 16 by a strained right calf, Judge went to the Yankees’ Double-A ballpark in Somerset, New Jersey, for live batting practice Wednesday as he tries to work his way back from a leg injury to be available later in the postseason.
“Saturday’s a long ways away, but I’m doing everything I can, all morning, night, during the game, everything to prepare myself to be ready to go,” Judge said after Wednesday night’s 9-2 win. “So I want to be in there. So we’ll see what happens.”
Judge did not join teammates along the first-base line for introductions before the Yankees’ 9-0 win in Tuesday’s opener of the best-of-three series.
“I think he was getting treatment,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said.
Judge ran in the outfield before Tuesday night’s game and on Wednesday went to Somerset to hit. He returned to the Bronx in time to watch Game 2.
A three-time AL MVP, Judge was limited to 66 games this season. The 34-year-old slugger hit .241 with 18 homers, 41 RBIs and an .871 OPS, including .174 with one homer and three RBIs in September.
Left-hander Ryan Weathers, sidelined with a left forearm flexor strain since Aug. 22, was to throw a bullpen at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday.
Boone said right-hander Clarke Schmidt won’t pitch again this year. The 30-year-old relieved on Sept. 16 at Minnesota in his first big league appearance since Tommy John surgery on July 11, 2025, then was put on the injured list with right biceps inflammation.

item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Regardless of how his career turns out, Chicago Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong may already have Mike Trout beat in one key category: playoff games. Both are still seeking their first Championship Series appearance, but at least PCA had another opportunity this week. Any hopes the Cubs had of advancing beyond the Wild Card Round ended fairly quickly, though, with the presumptive NL MVP being held hitless in eight at-bats against the Padres. Crow-Armstrong’s dreadful two-game performance follo
item.content:encoded:
Regardless of how his career turns out, Chicago Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong may already have Mike Trout beat in one key category: playoff games.
Both are still seeking their first Championship Series appearance, but at least PCA had another opportunity this week. Any hopes the Cubs had of advancing beyond the Wild Card Round ended fairly quickly, though, with the presumptive NL MVP being held hitless in eight at-bats against the Padres.
Crow-Armstrong’s dreadful two-game performance follows him hitting .184 with 12 strikeouts over eight playoff games last year.
“You can look at the scoreboard, you can look at the stat sheet, wherever you get your numbers from, and it is clear to see that I didn’t contribute,” he told reporters. “None of it feels good. Pretty disappointed in myself, but that’s for me to work on.”
Given the current state of baseball’s labor crisis, he’ll likely have plenty of additional time to reflect on what went wrong.
Should Chicago Cubs fans be concerned by Pete Crow-Armstrong’s playoff struggles?
Some of the more generous PCA-related social media posts have involved questioning his MVP status or accusing him of being overrated. Right, because someone who just put up nearly 10 bWAR and joined the 40-40 club is overrated.
This will sound crazy, but Crow-Armstrong is still only 24. He’s already become one of the sport’s premier faces to the point that we wouldn’t be shocked if he’s on the cover of next year’s MLB The Show game. We talk so much about New York and Los Angeles that we forget he’s thrived in the Chicago media market, which isn’t exactly a bunch of villages and huts in the middle of nowhere.
Anyone who blames Crow-Armstrong for the Cubs’ playoff loss is deliberately being lazy. Alex Bregman, Dansby Swanson and Ian Happ all went hitless in the series themselves. They managed one run over 18 innings.
Credit to the Padres for keeping Crow-Armstrong off the basepaths, which should sound obvious enough. But he drew walks in nearly 12 percent of his plate appearances during the regular season yet only managed a single free pass this week.
Analysts constantly referenced Trout’s 1-for-12 showing in the 2014 ALDS — still his lone postseason appearance — because he and the Angels still haven’t returned to the playoffs. That’s why no one even bothers bringing it up anymore; we’ve just collectively gotten used to the Angels finishing in or near last place.
Do you remember who else had a reputation as a poor postseason performer? Alex Rodriguez, a narrative that vanished when the Yankees won the 2009 World Series. The talk surrounding Aaron Judge’s October struggles will vanish if he catches the final out of the Fall Classic.
Let’s give Crow-Armstrong some more time. Besides, the Cubs are only 10 years into a title drought rather than 108. Things could be far worse.

item.title: [Yardbarker] Yankees’ Spencer Jones Makes MLB History With Incredible Feat
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: New York Yankees outfielder Spencer Jones already looked like an outlier before he stepped into the batter’s box in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the American League Wild Card Series. The Yankees rookie is 6-foot-7, plays center field, runs better than a frame that size usually allows, and carries a batting stance that draws comparisons to Shohei Ohtani. On Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium, he added a line to the record book that no one else has occupied in more than a century of searchable pla
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees outfielder Spencer Jones already looked like an outlier before he stepped into the batter’s box in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the American League Wild Card Series.
The Yankees rookie is 6-foot-7, plays center field, runs better than a frame that size usually allows, and carries a batting stance that draws comparisons to Shohei Ohtani.
On Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium, he added a line to the record book that no one else has occupied in more than a century of searchable play-by-play.
Jones led off the sixth against Garrett Crochet, the Red Sox ace working in relief for the first time in months. The at-bat ended with a swing and a miss on a pitch in the dirt.
A third strike that the catcher does not hold is not automatically an out, and Adley Rutschman could not keep the ball. Jones took off for first. The call on the field went against him. Replay did not. The out was overturned, and a strikeout that should have ended the plate appearance instead put the tallest man in the Yankees lineup on base.
From there the inning got stranger. Jones stole second, tacking a stolen base onto a strikeout that had not counted as an out. He later came around to score. New York kept hitting.
The Yankees batted all the way around, and Jones found himself in the box again before the sixth was over. This time the strikeout stuck. There was no wild pitch, no errant throw, no second life. He was out.
The combination is what makes the sequence historic.
According to Baseball Reference researcher Katie Sharp, Jones is the first player in major-league history, regular season or postseason, to record two strikeouts and a stolen base in the same inning.
The play-by-play record used for that search reaches back to 1910. In more than a hundred years of games, including every October series that has been logged the same way, nobody had done it.
The oddity landed inside a series New York has controlled without its captain. Aaron Judge has been unavailable, and the Yankees still won the first two games against Boston by scores of 9-0 and 9-2. Jones is not Judge, and nobody in the organization is pretending otherwise.
He is, though, another 6-foot-7 outfielder with real power, and he just turned a pair of strikeouts into a run and a stolen base in a playoff inning.
That does not decide a series against the Tampa Bay Rays, the American League’s top seed, if New York advances. It does suggest a club that has found ways to convert messy moments into something useful.
The franchise has not won a World Series since 2009. An inning that had never happened before is not a championship. It is a reminder that this October, even the failures have not stayed failures for long.

item.content:encoded:
Colin Cowherd's Aaron Judge take will catch Yankees fans' attention appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees recently punched their ticket to the ALDS with a comfortable home win over the rival Boston Red Sox in Game 2 of the Wild Card series, sweeping that matchup and moving on to the next round. The Yankees won this series without superstar Aaron Judge, who is still recovering from an injury suffered toward the end of the regular season.
Recently, sports media personality Colin Cowherd of FS1 weighed in on Judge with a hot take.
"Aaron Judge didn't play. Stanton didn't play. None of it mattered when you have two phenomenal pitching performances. They're not just Aaron Judge reliant anymore," said Cowherd, via Herd w/Colin Cowherd on X, formerly Twitter.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
While the Yankees certainly didn't need Judge to make quick work of the Red Sox this week, or stay afloat in the AL standings overall this year, they will more than likely need him back in order to have any realistic chance of making a run at the World Series this year, starting with their upcoming matchup against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Judge missed the majority of this season due to a ribcage injury and had only recently returned from that issue when he went down with a separate ailment, sidelining him for the Red Sox matchup and having some fans wondering if the season would crash and burn before the traditional playoffs even got underway.
However, now that the team has punched its ticket to the ALDS, fans will be scouring the internet for positive injury updates on Judge prior to Game 1.
In any case, the Rays and Yankees are set to get their series underway on Saturday at 6:30 pm ET from Tampa Bay.
Related: Why Red Sox fan Dave Portnoy called out Yankees after AL Wild Card Series

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Aaron Judge Gives Personal Injury Update Ahead of ALDS vs. Rays
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The New York Yankees have punched their ticket to the ALDS after defeating the Boston Red Sox 9-2 in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series on Wednesday night. They outscored Boston 18-2 across the two games they played, and both of the Red Sox runs came off solo home runs. Aaron Judge Gives Personal Update on Injury Following the Yankees' win
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have punched their ticket to the ALDS after defeating the Boston Red Sox 9-2 in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series on Wednesday night.
They outscored Boston 18-2 across the two games they played, and both of the Red Sox runs came off solo home runs.
Now, the Yankees are set for another real challenge as they'll begin a best-of-five series against the No. 1-seeded Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Saturday.
Aaron Judge Gives Personal Update on Injury
Following the Yankees' win, superstar Aaron Judge spoke to the media and gave a brief update on the calf injury that ultimately kept him off the 26-man roster for the Wild Card Series.
Now that the series is over, the Yankees can submit an entirely new roster for the ALDS, which could include Judge if they deem him healthy enough to play.
Judge, however, said that he did not run the bases at Somerset on Wednesday and hasn't run the bases yet, which is likely one of the major steps in his rehab. He noted that he's working every day toward a return.
"My job is to continue to get ready. That's what I've been doing every day," Judge said postgame.
Aaron Judge, while dodging champagne spritzes, said that he did not run the bases in Somerset today.
He didn’t have anything to say about his potential availability for the ALDS, other than, “My job is to continue to get ready. That’s what I’ve been doing every day.” #Yankees https://t.co/5GhWIRVrd3
— Gary Phillips (@GaryHPhillips) October 1, 2026
How Can Judge Play in ALDS?
For Judge to be eligible to play in the ALDS, the Yankees would obviously need to activate him and then add him to the 26-man roster before Saturday's game.
However, doing that would mean removing another player. Given that New York already went hitter-heavy with its pitcher-to-batter ratio for the Wild Card roster, it would likely be one of its bench bats, such as Amed Rosario or Jose Caballero. If they choose to keep the infield depth, it would have to be one of the outfielders, such as Heliot Ramos, Trent Grisham, or Spencer Jones.
The team added Giancarlo Stanton to the Wild Card roster, but he made no appearances. So, it's possible they could add Judge and let him continue rehabbing for Games 1 and 2 before bringing him back when the series heads to New York.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Spencer Jones’ hustle ignites game-breaking rally for Yankees to eliminate Red Sox

item.description: When you look at Spencer Jones, you don’t necessarily think of speed. The 6-foot-7 giant is equipped with light-tower power, as you would expect from someone of his size. However, it was his blazing speed that jump-started the Yankees‘ crucial rally in their 9-2 series-clinching win over the Red Sox on Thursday night. The outfielder struck out swinging against Garrett Crochet in the bottom of the sixth, however, the ball skirted just a few feet away from Adley Rutschman, allowing Jones to attemp
item.content:encoded:
When you look at Spencer Jones, you don’t necessarily think of speed.
The 6-foot-7 giant is equipped with light-tower power, as you would expect from someone of his size. However, it was his blazing speed that jump-started the Yankees‘ crucial rally in their 9-2 series-clinching win over the Red Sox on Thursday night.
The outfielder struck out swinging against Garrett Crochet in the bottom of the sixth, however, the ball skirted just a few feet away from Adley Rutschman, allowing Jones to attempt to reach on a dropped third strike. The 25-year-old just beat out the throw to kick off the six-run rally that was capped off by Cody Bellinger’s three-run blast.
Jones was initially ruled out, but manager Aaron Boone successfully challenged the play.
“Yeah, great. I mean, I couldn’t believe he was there,” said Boone. “I saw the ball squirt away a little bit. I didn’t think that much of it, and looked up and I was, like, oh, he’s safe.
“He got down there really good. You guys have covered us have seen Spencer run. When he gets it going, he can really go. But great job there. And then the stolen base gets to third, sets us up to get a tack-on run, and then we get some big plays.”
It shouldn’t have come as a surprise to Boone that Jones beat the throw, as he’s been touted for his speed. The neophyte ranked in the 88th percentile in sprint speed this season at 28.9 feet per second, according to Baseball Savant.
The rookie is playing a crucial role for the Yankees as their starting center fielder. Jones batted fourth for the club on Wednesday night against starter Sonny Gray and will likely continue to bat in the middle of the order against right-handed pitching.
The former top prospect earned his role this postseason with a stellar second stint in the big leagues during the regular season. Jones struggled during his first stretch in the bigs as he slashed .167/.259/.167 before being demoted after just 10 games in May. He was recalled just a few weeks later and posted a .253/.318/.456 slashline with 11 homers, 38 RBI and nine stolen bases, remaining a staple in the lineup for the rest of the season — with his legs and glove as well.
Jones performed respectably in his first taste of postseason baseball, going 2-for-8 with two runs scored in the games against the Red Sox. The homegrown kids somewhat stole the show in the first round, as fellow draft picks Ben Rice, Cam Schlittler, George Lombard Jr. and Austin Wells also had very strong series.
“Yeah, it’s super fun,” said Rice. “All of us came up with one another in a way. There was some overlap. Maybe a couple guys were ahead of others. But now we’re all here in the big leagues. And it’s been so cool seeing each guy have success and carve out their own role.
“Definitely a tight-knit group, and we take pride in that.”
The Yankees will need more from their youngsters if they want to advance past the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS beginning Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are moving on!!
They will face the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series, beginning this weekend.
As Aaron Judge's status is still in limbo, other players will need to step up. If manager Aaron Boone pencils Anthony Volpe in the lineup during the ALDS, he could be a difference-maker.
Recently, FanSided.com contributors made a bold Anthony Volpe prediction, and it's pretty positive.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Trade Prediction Lands 2X MLB All-Star Infielder
Anthony Volpe Predicted to Have Impact at 3B for Yankees
With George Lombard Jr. manning the reins at shortstop, if Anthony Volpe sees himself in the lineup, it will either be at third base or second.
Volpe's arm doesn't play well at third base, but that didn't stop the speculation, as the Yankees would also look much better on paper with Volpe at 3B over Ryan McMahon.
FanSided MLB director Adam Weinrib recently made the bold prediction that Volpe will be an impact player at 3B:
"The Yankees turned to Volpe out of sheer desperation, due to both Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s injury and Ryan McMahon's ineffectiveness, and the one-time punching bag was actually … pretty good in September? The offense is unremarkable but still worlds better than McMahon, and his defense has been fine at third base. New York is going to need him in October."
Anthony Volpe was in the lineup for game one against the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card round, but that was with a left-hander on the mound. Manager Boone has had a clear strategy when it comes to stacking the lineup with favorite hitting matchups, according to whoever the opposing starter is.
More MLB on Heavy: Houston Astros Predicted to Cut Ties with Manager Joe Espada After Quick White Sox Series
Anthony Volpe's 2026 Season At a Glance
You have to give Anthony Volpe a lot of credit for the way he's handled the 2026 season.
He started the year on the IL, which led to him not really having a starting spot in the infield, and Volpe was eventually demoted to the minors for a long stretch of the season.
After an injury to Jazz Chisholm Jr., Volpe stepped up in a few clutch moments in September for the Yankees, and he's now back in the fold, with Chisholm and Volpe platooning at 2B.
However, New York Yankees fans would be very pleased if this Anthony Volpe prediction could come to life over the next few weeks.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Former Yankees Manager Reveals Potential Plan for Aaron Judge

item.description: The New York Yankees were able to complete a two-game sweep of the Boston Red Sox without Aaron Judge, but in order to make a World Series run, you can bet they'll need their captain back in the lineup. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees were able to complete a two-game sweep of the Boston Red Sox without Aaron Judge, but in order to make a World Series run, you can bet they'll need their captain back in the lineup.
But when could that happen?
Judge suffered a calf strain on Sept. 16, an injury that was ruled "moderate." The injury also occurred in the soleus muscle, which is connected to the Achilles tendon. Understandably, the Yankees are being extra cautious.
Just over two weeks have passed since Judge was first injured, and typically, moderate strains can take a month-and-a-half to two months to heal.
New York doesn't have that much time.
So could Judge actually return as soon as the Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays?
The Yankees will open up Game 1 of the ALDS this Saturday, and considering Judge hasn't even run the bases yet, a return in the opener seems slim to none.
However, former New York manager Joe Girardi has proposed a scenario in which the Yanks could put Judge on the ALDS roster, sit him for the first couple of games and then potentially play him later on in the series.
The Yankees did something similar with Giancarlo Stanton in the Wild Card Series. Stanton was healthy enough to make the roster, but New York didn't actually have to use him as it outscored the Red Sox 18-2 over the course of the two-game sweep.
Of course, that concept becomes a bit riskier over the course of a longer series where you might need some more pitching.
Unlike the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-3, the Division Series is a best-of-5, so the Yankees have to be careful in how they go about constructing their roster.
Stanton will certainly be on the roster again. He has been transitioned into a pinch-hitting role for New York for his lethal October bat alone. So can the Yankees find room for Judge?
In the Wild Card Series, New York employed 16 position players and 10 pitchers. It remains to be seen how Aaron Boone goes about allocating his 26-man group for the ALDS, but there is absolutely a chance he features more pitching.
One thing is for sure: even if Judge does play, he won't be in right field. He would DH, which would move Ben Rice into a full-time role at first base and send Luis Garcia Jr. to the bench. Not a bad bat to have off the pine.
All that being said, we'll see what Boone ultimately decides ahead of Game 1. If he feels Judge isn't even close, he might not even put him on the roster.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Max Fried joins MLB playoff legends with his start vs Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers

Tonight, Max Fried will become the sixth pitcher in MLB history to make at least one postseason start in seven consecutive years (2020-2026), joining Greg Maddux (nine), Andy Pettitte (nine), Tom Glavine (eig
item.content:encoded:
Max Fried added his name to an exclusive list of MLB postseason legends Wednesday night. The Yankees left-hander became the seventh pitcher in MLB history to make at least one postseason start in seven consecutive years, joining some of the greatest playoff pitchers the sport has ever seen.
Tonight, Max Fried will become the sixth pitcher in MLB history to make at least one postseason start in seven consecutive years (2020-2026), joining Greg Maddux (nine), Andy Pettitte (nine), Tom Glavine (eight), Clayton Kershaw (eight) and Roger Clemens (seven). pic.twitter.com/ZDBRWyYOoN
— OptaSTATS (@OptaSTATS) September 30, 2026
Fried joins an incredible list of postseason legends
Fried’s streak began in 2020 and continued through Wednesday night’s Game 2 start against the Boston Red Sox. That gives him seven consecutive seasons with at least one postseason start, putting him alongside an impressive group of pitchers.
The list includes Tom Glavine, Greg Maddux, Andy Pettitte, Clayton Kershaw, John Smoltz and Roger Clemens.
Fried’s achievement is particularly notable because he has now established himself as a consistent postseason starter across multiple organizations and stages of his career.
Fried delivered when the Yankees needed him
Fried didn’t simply make history by taking the mound. He delivered one of his best postseason performances in a Yankees uniform.
The left-hander allowed just three hits and one earned run over six innings against Boston, walking one and striking out six on 98 pitches. The Yankees went on to win 9-2 and complete a two-game sweep of the Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series.
After the Yankees selected Cam Schlittler to start Game 1, Fried followed him in Game 2 and helped send New York into the AL Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
For Fried, Wednesday night was another chapter in an already impressive postseason résumé — and another reminder that his October experience now puts him in the company of some legendary MLB playoff pitchers.

item.content:encoded:
It was always inevitable that Cam Schlittler would continue his feud with Red Sox fans and Boston-based media outlets.
Following the blowout 9-2 win on Wednesday night that clinched the Yankees' slot in the ALDS, Schlittler was easy to find in the comments on the Yankees' celebratory social media post. The Walpole, Massachusetts native had some choice words in response to some earlier comments made about his career stats against the Red Sox.
Schlittler's comment, "Wat the 4's gotta say now," is a clapback at some personalities from New England sports media personality Jared Carrabis' podcast 'Section 10.'
To provide a bit more context, Rusey, one of the personalities on the podcast, previously called Schlittler ugly and essentially useless, even after dominating Boston in the final rivalry matchup of the regular season. He could've taken the high road in celebratory fashion on Wednesday night, but he seemingly found that choice too boring and let the fans stay mad.
Schlittler had an outstanding performance to completely shut down Boston in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series on Tuesday night. Pitching through six and a third scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts, the Yankees' ace has accumulated a 0.47 ERA in his first six career starts against the Red Sox. He's the fourth pitcher in MLB postseason history with two 10-strikeout games before turning 26.
The Yankees' postseason run hasn't seen the last of Schlittler, as he will likely take the mound for the second game of the best-of-five Division Series against Tampa Bay, with a chance to start in Game 5 as well should it go the distance. Securing the Wild Card Series in two games allows for an extra day of rest before the Yankees travel down to face the Rays.
Coverage for Game 1 of the ALDS begins Saturday at 6:30 p.m. EST.

item.title: [bolavip.com] Brian Cashman, NY Yankees’ front office earn shoutout from Gerrit Cole after eliminating Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Federico O'donnell
item.description: Much was said about the New York Yankees and the way the front office, led by general manager Brian Cashman, went about its business at the trade deadline. Many believed the Bronx Bombers didn’t do enough to truly compete in the 2026 MLB Postseason, but that was proven wrong in the AL Wild Card against the Boston Red Sox—despite Aaron Judge’s absence. Amid the champagne celebration, starting pitcher Gerrit Cole voiced an honest assessment of the work done behind closed doors by the front office.
item.content:encoded:
Much was said about the New York Yankees and the way the front office, led by general manager Brian Cashman, went about its business at the trade deadline. Many believed the Bronx Bombers didn’t do enough to truly compete in the 2026 MLB Postseason, but that was proven wrong in the AL Wild Card against the Boston Red Sox—despite Aaron Judge’s absence. Amid the champagne celebration, starting pitcher Gerrit Cole voiced an honest assessment of the work done behind closed doors by the front office.
Although the true test will come when the Yankees play the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS next, the way the squad in The Bronx has been assembled clearly didn’t go unnoticed by Cole, who praised Cashman and the Yankees’ brass after the 2-0 series win over the Red Sox.
“You’ve got to go out and buy the tools. The roster looks really good at this point. We’re very competitive, and we have a lot of different ways that we can beat you. A lot of credit goes to a lot of people in this building,” Cole stated, via Chris Kirschner of The Athletic.
NY Yankees’ lineup depth proves decisive
It’s a new day in New York, more specifically in The Bronx. Indeed, the Yankees would love to have Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton back at the plate, but they have figured things out even without those two power bats.
Gerrit Cole #45 of the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium.
New York is no longer a home-run-dependent creature in the MLB Playoffs. The Yankees are now a depth monster, ready to drown out opponents with lengthy, grueling innings, especially when playing at home at Yankee Stadium.
Yankees’ perfect 6th inning in Game 2
It remains to be seen how this strategy stacks up against the AL East-winning Rays, but it wreaked havoc against the Red Sox. The bottom of the sixth inning in Game 2 was Aaron Boone’s team’s magnum opus so far in the postseason. The Yankees made the most of every single thing the Red Sox gave them.
A wild pitch? Spencer Jones would run his way to first. Another bad throw, and he stole two bases, setting up shop at third. From there on, the Yankees’ batters simply kept the base hits coming until it was Cody Bellinger’s turn at the plate.
The Red Sox picked their poison: They intentionally walked Ben Rice to first base. Bellinger needed just one changeup from Garrett Whitlock to decipher the code. On the second pitch, he went yard, calling game in the process as New York jumped to a game-sealing, series-ending 8-1 lead.
NY Yankees are for real in 2026 postseason
It was the perfect demonstration of how the entire lineup can come together to decide postseason games for the Pinstripers. If they could, the Yankees would hang it up on a wall at Yankee Stadium, but they don’t do that in The Bronx.
All they care about is winning the World Series, and this Yankees team, with a different recipe from years past, confirmed it can be a serious contender for the Commissioner’s Trophy in 2026. And that’s even without Judge.
Lastly, Brian Cashman, who’s been through the wringer and at the receiving end of fans’ criticism time and again, deserves credit. It’s still early for victory laps, but Cole’s shoutout to the front office’s work was well deserved.
Key takeaways
- Brian Cashman received praise from Gerrit Cole after New York eliminated Boston.
- The Yankees beat the Red Sox 2-0 in the AL Wild Card series.
- Cody Bellinger hit a game-sealing home run in the sixth inning of Game 2.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Sequence of the Week: Cam Schlittler (9/29)
